The Mix window's plugin insert menu lists third-party plugins as one flat column per format. title: Shared audio engine with FPGA backend for low-latency monitoring, AES67 and ST 2110
author: marcnnn
body:
## Summary

A proposal to give SoundCraft and FilmCraft **one shared audio engine**, with a pluggable device backend. Any computer can use the normal OS backend, and an **FPGA audio-over-IP card** can be added as an optional backend for:

- **Low-latency monitoring** during recording and production (cue mixes and headphone feeds processed on the card, a few samples of latency)
- **AES67 / SMPTE ST 2110-30** recording and playback, with ST 2110-20 video playout and ingest for FilmCraft later
- **Sample-accurate sync** between SoundCraft and FilmCraft on one machine, and between machines via PTP (IEEE 1588)

The FilmCraft side (sync, playout, ingest) is tracked in storytold/filmcraft#327.

This issue is for discussion. It doesn't ask for anything to be built right away.

## Motivation

Today both apps follow the classic model: the audio device is the master clock, and each callback from cpal moves the timeline forward by one buffer. That works well for a single app on a single machine. It falls short in three places:

1. **Monitoring latency.** A software DAW can't monitor with less latency than its buffer size, however well it's written. Pro Tools HDX, UAD Apollo and RME TotalMix solve this by mixing the monitor feeds in hardware. An open equivalent doesn't exist.
2. **Inter-app sync.** FilmCraft and SoundCraft each count callbacks from their own device. Keeping them aligned means passing positions over IPC or MTC, and they drift between updates.
3. **IP media.** AES67 and ST 2110 identify each sample and frame by absolute network time (PTP, mapped by SMPTE ST 2059-1). A timeline that only counts callbacks can't produce or consume those timestamps directly.

## Proposal

### 1. A shared engine with two clients

```
 SoundCraft UI        FilmCraft UI
      \                  /
       shared audio engine  (graph, transport, clock, recording)
        |               |
  generic backend    FPGA backend
  (cpal: ALSA,       (DMA rings, PTP hardware clock, on-card mixer,
 …

title: Windows: all Cmd+ keyboard shortcuts do nothing (Ctrl+A, Ctrl+B, Ctrl+Space, …)
author: MacquarieP
body:
## Summary
On Windows, none of the shortcuts defined with `Cmd` in the command registry fire. For example, Ctrl+A (Select All), Ctrl+B (Clear), Ctrl+X (Cut), Ctrl+Space (Record) and Ctrl+Shift+I (Import Audio) all do nothing. The same commands work from the menu bar. Shortcuts without `Cmd` (e.g. Space, Shift+R) work.

## Environment
- Windows 11 x64
- Built from source at `c51e5d5` (2026-10-08) with `cargo run --release -p soundcraft`

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create an audio track and record or import a clip.
2. Press Ctrl+A, then Ctrl+B.
3. Nothing happens. Edit → Select All, then Edit → Clear, from the menu bar works.

## Cause
`mods_match` in `crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs` (line 44):

```rust
fn mods_match(want: Modifiers, got: Modifiers) -> bool {
    want.command == got.command && want.shift == got.shift && want.alt == got.alt && (want.ctrl == got.ctrl || got.mac_cmd)
}
```

For a `Cmd+…` shortcut, `parse` sets `want.command = true`, `want.ctrl = false`. On Windows and Linux, egui reports the Ctrl key as `command = true` **and** `ctrl = true`, and `mac_cmd` is always false. So `want.ctrl == got.ctrl` is `false == true`, and the match fails for every `Cmd` shortcut.

## Suggested fix
Treat Ctrl as satisfied when the shortcut asks for `Cmd` on non-macOS platforms:

```rust
fn mods_match(want: Modifiers, got: Modifiers) -> bool {
    // On Windows/Linux, "Cmd" is the Ctrl key, so Ctrl is expected to be held too.
    let ctrl_ok = want.ctrl == got.ctrl || got.mac_cmd || (want.command && !want.ctrl && !cfg!(target_os = "macos"));
    want.command == got.command && want.shift == got.shift && want.alt == got.alt && ctrl_ok
}
```

A unit test that builds `Modifiers { ctrl: true, command: true, ..Default::default() }` and checks it matches `parse("Cmd+A")` would cover this on all platforms.

`Cmd+Ctrl+…` shortcuts (e.g. `Cmd+Ctrl+X`, Cut Clip Gain) can't be told apart from `Cmd+…` on Windows, since both are just Ctrl. They may need a Windows-specific mapping (e.g. …

title: Record-enable forces input monitoring with no opt-out, causing feedback with virtual audio routing (VoiceMeeter); no input device selection
author: MacquarieP
body:
## Summary
On Windows with VoiceMeeter (a common setup for recording system audio), recording in SoundCraft produces a take full of feedback: a high-pitched whine, crackling, and a level that climbs until it clips. Two design choices combine to cause it, and neither can be changed from the UI:

1. **Arming a track always turns on input monitoring.** There's no setting to record without hearing the input through SoundCraft's output.
2. **Recording always uses the Windows default input device.** There's no input selector, so you can't choose which VoiceMeeter bus to record or move the input away from the output path.  (this use of voicemeeter is very popular and allows certain recordings  - Cable and Voicemeeter work together. it may need a little research to work through the issue)

## Environment
- Windows 11 x64, built from source at `c51e5d5` (2026-10-08)
- VoiceMeeter (standard edition) + VB-Audio Virtual Cable
- Playback Engine shows: Output = CABLE Input (VB-Audio Virtual Cable), Input = VoiceMeeter Output (VoiceMeeter VAIO), 2 ch @ 48 kHz, session 48 kHz

## Routing
- Windows default playback = CABLE Input. SoundCraft plays here.
- VoiceMeeter Stereo Input 1 = CABLE Output, sent to A (speakers) and B (VoiceMeeter Output).
- Windows default recording = VoiceMeeter Output (B bus). SoundCraft records from here.

B has to be on for Stereo Input 1 so that audio playing through the cable can be recorded. That's the normal way to record system audio with VoiceMeeter, and it works fine in Adobe Audition, which doesn't monitor through its own output by default.

## What happens
As soon as a track is armed, SoundCraft plays the input back out: B → SoundCraft monitor → CABLE Input → Stereo Input 1 → B → … This closes a loop.

Analysis of a 22.5 s take (bounced as 24-bit WAV):
- The energy is concentrated at about 5–10 kHz, with peaks at 5.9 kHz and 7.5 kHz, dozens of dB above the programme material.
- Autocorrelation shows a strong period of 1,200 samples (25 ms), the lo…

title: Linux (Fedora/GNOME): UI symbols show as empty boxes, and the window title bar doesn't match the desktop
author: fqazzazee
body:
## Environment

- Fedora 44, GNOME Shell 50.5, Wayland session, 167% display scaling
- Built from source at `eac0edd`

## Title bar doesn't follow the GNOME theme (Wayland)

On GNOME Wayland, the app draws its own title bar. This app shows winit's plain fallback bar, which
ignores the GNOME theme, dark mode and button layout.

The workspace sets `eframe = { version = "0.36", default-features = false }` (`Cargo.toml:45`),
which also drops winit's default `wayland-csd-adwaita` feature, so `sctk-adwaita` isn't in
`Cargo.lock`.

Possible fixes:

- Enable `winit/wayland-csd-adwaita`, so the title bar follows GNOME's look and light/dark mode, or
- Draw an in-app title bar, as PhotoCraft does on Linux.

Workaround: start the app through Xwayland (`env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY soundcraft`), so GNOME draws a real
title bar.

Same issue in GridCraft, with more detail: https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/54

## Symbols show as empty boxes on Fedora

`crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs` looks for DejaVu Sans and Liberation Sans only at Debian/Arch paths
(for example `/usr/share/fonts/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf`). Fedora installs them at
`/usr/share/fonts/dejavu-sans-fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf` and
`/usr/share/fonts/liberation-sans-fonts/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf`, so the UI falls back to egui's
built-in fonts. These characters used in `crates/ui-egui/src` are missing from those fonts:

`→ ▸ ▾ ♯ ✕`

DejaVu Sans has all of them. Adding the Fedora folder names, or asking fontconfig for the font
(`fc-match`), would fix it. The GridCraft issue above covers the same problem.

title: `convert` and `--bounce` write WAV data to any file extension (.mp3, .ogg, .m4a, .aac, .opus, .xyz) and report success
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

According to the README, MP3, Ogg Vorbis and AAC are input-only, and export supports WAV, AIFF and FLAC. Despite that, `soundcraft-cli convert in.wav out.mp3` prints `wrote out.mp3 (…)` and exits 0. The file is actually 24-bit PCM WAV with a `.mp3` name. `run --bounce mix.mp3` behaves the same way. Users and agents end up with mislabeled files, and players or uploaders that trust the extension reject them or play noise. Unknown extensions like `.xyz` are also accepted silently.

**Environment**
- SoundCraft `main` @ eac0edd (v0.3.0), `soundcraft-cli` release build
- Linux x86_64 (Debian 13), Rust 1.99; checked with ffprobe 7.1

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav t.mp3        # "wrote t.mp3 (2 ch, 48000 Hz, 3.00 s)", exit 0
ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=format_name:stream=codec_name -of csv=p=0 t.mp3   # pcm_s24le / wav
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav t.ogg        # also WAV inside
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav t.xyz        # also WAV, no warning
soundcraft-cli run --demo --bounce b.mp3     # bounce: WAV inside b.mp3
```
`.flac` and `.aiff` are written correctly.

**Expected**
For extensions it cannot encode, the command should fail with an error like "unsupported output format: mp3 (supported: wav, aiff, flac)" and a non-zero exit code. It should never write a file whose content doesn't match its extension.

**Actual**
A WAV file is written under the requested name and exit code 0 is returned. The JSON bounce report (`path: "b.mp3"`) also implies the file is an MP3.

title: `soundcraft-cli --help` prints a stray code fence and Rust source lines (`#![deny(...)]`, `use serde_json…`)
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

`--help` and `help` build the usage text with `include_str!("main.rs").lines().skip(3).take(14)` (`apps/soundcraft-cli/src/main.rs:53`). The doc block now has only 10 usage lines, so the output ends with the closing ```` ``` ```` fence, the `#![deny(clippy::…)]` attribute, a blank line and `use serde_json::{Value, json};`.

**Environment**
- SoundCraft `main` @ eac0edd (v0.3.0), `soundcraft-cli` release build, Linux x86_64

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
soundcraft-cli --help
```

**Expected**
Only the usage lines are printed.

**Actual**
The output ends with:
~~~
soundcraft-cli plugins                          list built-in plugins
```
#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]

use serde_json::{Value, json};
~~~

**Suggested fix**
Take lines until the closing ```` ``` ````, for example `.skip(3).take_while(|l| !l.starts_with("//! ```"))`, or use a `const USAGE: &str`.

title: fix(cli): opening a session with missing audio files exits 0 with no warning and bounces silence
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

When a `.scraft` session's audio files are missing (for example, only the session file was copied to a new folder), `soundcraft-cli run --in` opens it, reports nothing, and `file.bounce_mix` writes a silent WAV (peak, true peak and LUFS all -144) with exit status 0 and empty stderr. title: fix(bounce): named bus sources silently render the main mix
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`file.bounce_mix` advertises `source?: main|bus name`, but selecting an existing bus, an empty bus, or a nonexistent bus succeeds and writes the same audio as the main mix. A caller following command discovery can receive the whole mix when it requested a bus render, with no error indicating the selection was ignored.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the published CLI in a disposable working directory. All commands below were executed. The built-in demo contains a `Verb` bus, which `setup.io` lists.

```sh
soundcraft-cli describe file.bounce_mix
soundcraft-cli run --demo --cmd 'setup.io'
soundcraft-cli run --demo --cmd 'file.bounce_mix={"path":"verb.wav","source":"Verb","start":{"seconds":10},"end":{"seconds":11},"dither":false}'
soundcraft-cli run --demo --cmd 'file.bounce_mix={"path":"main.wav","source":"main","start":{"seconds":10},"end":{"seconds":11},"dither":false}'
soundcraft-cli run --demo --cmd 'file.bounce_mix={"path":"default.wav","start":{"seconds":10},"end":{"seconds":11},"dither":false}'

title: fix(import): file.import_audio advertises new_tracks but silently ignores it
author: coygeek

## Summary

The engine command registry advertises `new_tracks?: true` for `file.import_audio`, and both CLI `describe` and MCP `list_commands` expose it to callers. The handler never reads this parameter. Changing it between `false`, `true`, and omission has no effect on track placement, and successful calls give no warning that it was ignored. This report concerns agreement between the advertised command parameters and execution, without assuming a particular meaning for `false`.

## Runtime or environment

- Executed the official SoundCraft CLI 0.3.0 macOS universal binary on macOS arm64, Darwin 27.0.0. Binary SHA-256: `e18b55586c0b3732284a886f9d5ed6b3bb0321e3065243bb5b7c4f9601c3e1a6`.

- Inspected a fresh clone of current default branch `main` at `eac0edd896cd6bdf27c0cdd0f9f9158c8956248a`. Its engine, automation, CLI, and desktop app source directories have no differences from the release tag. Did not build or execute `main`; Linux and Windows were not measured.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the official CLI identified above in a disposable working directory. Each `run` below starts a fresh blank session. Generate a mono, 48 kHz, 16-bit WAV with 4,800 frames:

```sh

import math, struct, wave

title: Web build shows macOS shortcuts (Cmd+…) in menus on Windows 10
author: anjoismysign
body:
### Description
In the web build, menu items show macOS-style shortcuts (`Cmd+N`, `Cmd+Shift+W`, `Cmd+Alt+B`, …) even though I am running Windows 10, where `Ctrl` is the platform modifier.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Deploy `soundcraft-web-0.3.0.zip` as a static site (I unzipped it and deployed the exact contents to Netlify).
2. Open the site in Microsoft Edge on Windows 10.
3. Open the **File** menu.

### Expected behavior
Shortcuts are shown with Windows conventions (`Ctrl+N`, `Ctrl+Shift+W`, `Ctrl+Alt+B`, …), matching the OS/browser platform.

### Actual behavior
Shortcuts are shown as `Cmd+N`, `Cmd+Shift+W`, `Cmd+Alt+B`, etc. The same happens in the other menus (for example `Cmd+Shift+I` on Import > Audio…).

### Environment
- SoundCraft: web build `soundcraft-web-0.3.0.zip` from https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/releases/download/v0.3.0/soundcraft-web-0.3.0.zip
- Hosting: exact zip contents deployed to Netlify (static site)
- Browser: Microsoft Edge 154.0.4258.62 (Official build) (64-bit)
- OS: Windows 10 Home 22H2, build 19045.7725, 64-bit

### Additional context
- I have only checked how the labels are displayed. I have not verified whether the shortcuts themselves work with `Ctrl` on Windows.
- Source observation (skimmed, not verified): the shortcut strings appear to be hard-coded with `Cmd+` in `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs` and `crates/engine/src/cmd/*`, so some platform detection would be needed for the web target (where `cfg!(target_os = "macos")` is not meaningful).

title: Web build: File > Import > Audio… shows a free-text box instead of a file picker

body:

In the web build, **File > Import > Audio…** opens a small "Import Audio" dialog with a plain text field and OK/Cancel. I can type anything (I typed "i can write whatever I want") and there is no way to browse for or select an audio file from my computer.

### Expected behavior
The browser's file picker opens (for example via an `<input type="file">` or the File System Access API) so I can select one or more audio files from my computer.

### Actual behavior
An "Import Audio" dialog with a free-text field appears. There is no file chooser and no way to browse files. The field accepts arbitrary text.

- SoundCraft: web build `soundcraft-web-0.3.0.zip` from https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/releases/download/v0.3.0/soundcraft-web-0.3.0.zip

- Browser: Microsoft Edge 154.0.4258.62 (Official build) (64-bit)
- OS: Windows 10 Home 22H2, build 19045.7725, 64-bit

- I have not tested the desktop builds or macOS, so I do not know whether the desktop apps show a native file dialog here.

title: Add Ukrainian UI translation
author: dmatviichuk
body:
SoundCraft currently displays its menus, command search, editor/mixer controls and dialogs in English. Add Ukrainian as a selectable UI language, with English fallback and a system-language choice that detects Ukrainian on desktop and in the browser.

title: Add Light and System interface themes that follow the macOS light/dark appearance
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add Light and System interface themes to SoundCraft, with System following the macOS light/dark appearance live, so the app changes with the rest of the desktop when macOS switches appearance automatically.

## Problem to solve

macOS can switch between Light and Dark appearance automatically (System Settings → Appearance → Auto changes it at sunset and sunrise), and many Mac apps offer a "System" theme choice that tracks it.

SoundCraft has a single, hardcoded dark interface. `Tokens::get` in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` ignores its context and always returns `Tokens::DARK`, and Window → UI Customization offers interface scale, reduce motion and auto-update settings but no theme choice. The persisted `UiState` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` has no theme field.

SoundCraft has no light theme and no way to follow the OS, so it stays dark while macOS and other apps are in Light mode.

## Proposed behavior

Add a light interface theme, and a theme choice with three options: System, Light and Dark. Light and Dark fix the theme. System applies Light or Dark to match the current macOS appearance at launch and switches immediately when the OS appearance changes while the app is open. The saved choice stays System; only the displayed theme changes.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The app has a light interface theme that covers every surface it paints itself (edit and mix windows, tracks, meters, faders, rulers and transport), not only standard widgets, with readable contrast throughout.

3. With System selected, the app starts in the light theme when macOS is set to Light and in the dark theme when macOS is set to Dark.

title: Feature request: optional “Ableton Live–style” window layout preset
author: anjoismysign
body:
# Summary
Offer a selectable layout preset arranging the existing windows in a Live-like way, alongside the current Edit/Mix layout. It builds on Window > Configurations and Workspaces.

# Motivation
Users coming from Ableton Live (see #38) expect a particular arrangement: a browser or clip library panel on the left, the arrangement in the center, a mixer strip row, and a detail panel at the bottom for the selected clip or device.

# Proposal
A built-in layout preset (saved as a Window Configuration) that arranges the existing panels this way.
Selectable from the Window menu, with the current layout still the default.
Uses only existing SoundCraft windows and original artwork. No Ableton assets, icons or wording.

# Out of scope
Session View (clip launching) and new panels that don’t exist yet. Those are separate requests.

# Additional context
The Window menu already has Workspaces and Window Configurations.

title: Feature request: selectable “Ableton Live” keyboard shortcut preset
author: anjoismysign
body:
# Summary
Let users choose a keyboard shortcut preset (the current SoundCraft/Pro Tools-style one as default, and an optional “Ableton Live” preset) so people coming from Live can use familiar keys.

# Motivation
Many users coming from Ableton Live (see #38) already know its shortcuts. A preset would lower the barrier without changing the default experience.

# Proposal
Add a preset selector in Setup > Keyboard Shortcuts, with the current mapping as default.
Ship an “Ableton Live” preset that maps Live’s commonly used shortcuts onto the equivalent existing SoundCraft commands (transport, duplicate, split, loop, zoom, track/clip operations, etc.).
Commands with no SoundCraft equivalent are simply skipped. This request doesn’t ask for Session View or a UI redesign.
Presets must be original mappings: no Ableton assets, icons, text or presets are copied.

# Out of scope
Session View, Live’s UI layout and Live-specific features. Those belong in the broader discussion in #38.

# Additional context
I’m only suggesting key mappings, since SoundCraft’s commands already carry shortcuts in the command registry.

title: MCP batch: `keep_going` hides failures (isError false)
author: salignatmoandal
body:
## Summary

The MCP `batch` tool continues after errors when `keep_going` is true, but still returns `isError: false` for the whole tool result. Agents that only check `isError` treat a partially failed batch as success.

Also, a non-array `calls` value is silently treated as `[]` and succeeds.

## Steps to reproduce

Via `soundcraft-cli mcp --demo` (`tools/call`):

```json
{"name":"batch","arguments":{"keep_going":true,"calls":[
  {"command":"track.new","params":{"count":1}},
  {"command":"mix.volume","params":{"track":"Nope","db":-6}}
]}}
```

And:

```json
{"name":"batch","arguments":{"calls":{"command":"track.new"}}}
```

## Expected

- Partial failure → tool result `isError: true` (payload still lists per-call `ok`/`error`); earlier successful commands remain applied when `keep_going` is true.
- Non-array `calls` → `isError: true` with a clear message.

## Actual

- `keep_going: true` + failed call → `isError: false` and an array mixing `ok: true/false`.
- Non-array `calls` → `isError: false`, `[]`.

## Evidence

`crates/automation/src/mcp.rs` batch arm:

```rust
if failed && !keep { Err(...) } else { Ok(json!(out)) }
```

and `as_array().cloned().unwrap_or_default()`.

author: fernandodilland

## TL;DR
Pro Tools has Auto Backup and Avid Cloud Collaboration. Please add an open equivalent: a "Save target" where the (small) session is backed up and versioned, the (huge, immutable) audio is uploaded once, and sessions can be handed off or checked out per track. Same root cause as storytold/craft-launcher#126 (opened the same day) and storytold/lightcraft#471 (fixed there by #484). title: fix(midi-editor): Quantize ignores the displayed musical grid
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The MIDI Editor's Quantize button uses sixteenth-note spacing even when the editor displays a quarter-note grid. Its tooltip promises quantization to the grid, but notes can move to positions between the displayed grid lines. Source inspection establishes this behavior for a valid MIDI clip; runtime reproduction was not run.

## Steps to reproduce

These steps describe a source-confirmed case on the pinned baseline and were not executed. Command calls below can use the running app's documented control interface or `SoundApp::run`.

title: fix(video): header validation uses unchecked arithmetic before rejecting invalid values
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Callers requesting an H.264 picture or parsing its headers are promised a normal error for invalid file data. Source inspection establishes that some header fields undergo unchecked arithmetic before their field limits run, so those error checks do not protect the arithmetic itself. This report concerns that ordinary correctness contract. Runtime behavior was not reproduced.

## Steps to reproduce

This is a complete static contract check at the pinned baseline, not an executed malformed-media reproduction. Trace decoder configuration and NAL dispatch into sequence parameter-set parsing. Compare the bit reader's encoding and representation checks with the parser's unchecked field normalization and subsequent semantic limit. The framing and identifier guards do not limit the independent field before that arithmetic. No crafted input or decoder execution is provided.

## Expected behavior

When file-derived header values cannot be normalized or are outside the supported field range, a caller receives an error before unsafe numeric use. Header validation preserves that result regardless of arithmetic-check settings. Supported valid movies continue to decode normally.

## Actual behavior

Source proves that the parser applies unchecked arithmetic before its field-specific error guard. The reader guarantees a representable unsigned value, which is insufficient to guarantee that subsequent normalization is representable. This violates the existing checked-number rule and leaves the promised error path unprotected at that operation. The native UI contains unwinding failures at the video-job level by resetting its worker. That catch does not validate the header or supply the direct parser's promised error result. The decoder's picture-job catch runs after header parsing and does not cover these operations.

author: Sirli01
body:
**Describe the bug**

Setting synth parameters (cutoff, amp envelope, level, etc.) via the MCP command `mix.instrument` returns success, and `track.save_preset` confirms the values are stored in the session — but the bounced audio is completely unaffected by the parameter values. The built-in synths effectively render with factory defaults no matter what is set.

**To reproduce**

1. Create an instrument track: `track.new` with `kind: "instrument"`, `instrument: "subtractive_synth"`

4. `track.save_preset` shows the new values are stored in the session state

title: mix.insert_params silently succeeds with unknown parameter names (set: 0)
author: Sirli01
body:
**Describe the bug**

`mix.insert_params` accepts arbitrary keys in its `params` object and reports overall success even when none of the keys match the plugin's actual parameters. Unknown keys are silently dropped; the only hint is the `set` count in the result. A typo like `gain_db` instead of `gain` looks identical to a successful call from the caller's perspective.

**To reproduce**

1. Add a gain insert: `mix.insert` with `plugin: "gain"`
2. Call `mix.insert_params` with `{track: 1, slot: 0, params: {gain_db: -14}}`

Result:

```json
{"ok": true, "set": 0}
```

The call reports `ok: true` while setting zero parameters — the actual key is `gain`, so nothing changed and no error or warning is returned.

3. Call it again with the correct key `{params: {gain: -14}}` → `{"ok": true, "set": 1}` and the gain changes.

**Expected behavior**

When some or all keys don't match known plugin parameters, the command should either fail or at least return which keys were ignored. `ok: true, set: 0` is indistinguishable from a successful no-op and is easy to miss when batching many calls.

**Suggestion**

- Return an error listing unrecognized keys (e.g. `unknown parameter(s): gain_db`), or
- Include the ignored key names in the result, or
- Also expose per-plugin parameter names via `list_commands`/introspection so MCP callers don't have to probe with `track.save_preset` to discover them.

**Environment**

Windows 10 (26300), driving the app via the bundled MCP server. Verified with the `gain` plugin; the general behavior appears to apply to all insert plugins.

title: CJK (Chinese) track names render blank in the Tracks panel
author: Sirli01
body:
**Describe the bug**

Track names containing CJK characters render as empty strings in the TRACKS panel (left sidebar). Mixed names like `主旋律Lead` display only the ASCII part (`Lead`); purely Chinese names like `幽灵回声` display nothing at all — the row appears unlabeled. The data itself is intact: `inspect_session` and the saved `.scraft` file both contain the correct Chinese names.

**To reproduce**

1. Create a track and name it with Chinese characters, e.g. `track.new` with `name: "主旋律Lead"`, and another with `name: "幽灵回声"`
2. Look at the TRACKS panel

Expected: full names render. Actual: the first shows `Lead`, the second shows an empty label. The track color bar and mute/solo indicators render normally.

**Additional context**

This looks like a rendering-layer issue rather than data corruption — no mojibake (e.g. `æä¸»...`) appears, the glyphs are simply dropped, which usually means the UI font/text renderer can't produce the glyphs or the string is passed through a code page that strips them. The session file stores the names correctly, so it's purely visual — but it makes the panel unusable for naming tracks in Chinese.

**Environment**

Windows 10 (26300), system locale zh-CN, app UI in English. Names set both via MCP (`track.new` / `track.rename`) and confirmed broken in the panel.

title: clip.loop creates detached copies: clip.unloop doesn't recognize them and note edits don't propagate
author: Sirli01
body:
## Summary

`clip.loop` produces **independent duplicate clips** rather than linked loop instances. Consequences:

- Note edits made on the source clip after looping never reach the copies (silently).
- `clip.unloop` rejects the result with `the selection is not a looped clip`, so the command pair is self-inconsistent.

## Environment

Windows 10, controlling via MCP `batch`, 48 kHz / 24-bit session, instrument tracks (subtractive_synth / drum_synth).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Track 1 has a 1-bar instrument clip (id 5, 0–96000 samples) with notes added via `midi.note_add`.
2. `clip.loop {clips: [5, 6, 7, 8], count: 4}` → `{loops: 12}`. `session.inspect` now shows 4 separate clips per track (ids 5, 9, 10, 11), each with its own note count.
3. `midi.note_edit {clip: 5, index: 1, length_ticks: 1100}` → returns ok, and `midi.notes {clip: 5}` confirms the new length.
4. `file.bounce_mix` over the last bar (the copy at 288000–384000) → **output is bit-identical to before the edit** (same LUFS/peak/file size). Repeating with different edits gives the same result, which initially looks like a stale render cache.
5. `midi.note_edit` applied directly to each copy (clips 9/10/11) → the bounce now changes. So rendering itself is fine; only the source→copy propagation is missing.
6. `clip.unloop {clips: [5]}` → error: `the selection is not a looped clip`.

## Expected behavior

Either loop instances are linked (edits propagate to all instances and `clip.unloop` collapses them), or — if `clip.loop` is intended as "duplicate N times" — the naming/behavior should be consistent (`clip.unloop` should still be able to clean up, or the semantics should be documented).

As-is it is a silent trap for API-driven workflows: a command named Loop whose output its own Unloop rejects, with edits that silently stop at the source clip.

title: edit.fades_create on instrument tracks: reports success and stores fade_out, but bounced audio ignores it
author: Sirli01
body:
## Summary

Creating a fade on an instrument (MIDI) track is accepted and stored in the session data, but has **no effect on the bounced audio** — a silent no-op.

## Environment

Windows 10, controlling via MCP `batch`, 48 kHz / 24-bit session, instrument track with `drum_synth`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Track 4 is an instrument track (`drum_synth`) with a 1-bar MIDI clip covering 288000–384000 samples.
2. `edit.fades_create {shape: exponential, tracks: [4], start: 381000, end: 384000}` → `{fades: 1}` (reported success).
3. `session.inspect` shows the clip now carries `"fade_out": 3000` — the property was stored.
4. `file.bounce_mix` over 288000–384000 → **output is bit-identical** to the bounce taken before the fade was created (same LUFS to 6 decimals, same peak, same file size).

To rule out caching: on the same session, muting a different track changes the bounce immediately, so bounces are not cached — the fade itself simply does not render.

## Expected behavior

Either fades should render on instrument/MIDI tracks, or `edit.fades_create` should reject or warn when targeting tracks whose audio cannot fade.

This is the same category of silent no-op as #266 (`mix.insert_params` reporting success for parameters that never apply): from the API surface, success + stored state + unchanged audio is indistinguishable from a working fade.

title: No UI way to create a MIDI clip on an empty instrument/MIDI track (midi.new_clip has no menu entry)
author: sajibsrs
body:
## Summary

On a new, empty instrument (or MIDI) track there is no way to create a MIDI clip from the UI, so a user can't enter notes by hand. The MIDI Editor shows *"Select a MIDI clip (or a MIDI track) to edit its notes."* and stays blank, even with the track selected.

The engine command `midi.new_clip` exists and works, but it has no menu path and no shortcut (`engine.commands` reports `"menu": []`), so it's only reachable from the control channel / CLI / MCP.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.5.0, macOS (aarch64)

## Steps to reproduce

1. **Track › New...** → kind *Instrument* (Subtractive Synth).
2. Try any of:
   - Pencil tool: click, double-click or drag on the empty track lane
   - Selector: select a range on the track, then **Edit › Consolidate** (returns `consolidated: 0`)
   - Right-click the empty lane (only offers *Paste*)
   - Select the track, open **MIDI EDITOR**, and click/drag with the Pencil in its area
3. Check `session.inspect`: the track still has `clips: []`.

## Expected

At least one UI path creates an empty MIDI clip, matching Pro Tools behaviour:
- Pencil drag (or click) on an empty MIDI/instrument track creates a clip of that length (or one bar), and/or
- Consolidate on an empty selection of a MIDI/instrument track creates an empty MIDI clip, and/or
- A menu item (e.g. *Clip › New MIDI Clip*) bound to `midi.new_clip`, and/or
- The MIDI Editor, when a MIDI/instrument track with no clips is selected, creates a clip on the first Pencil click.

Nothing happens; the only workaround is the control channel:

```sh
soundcraft-cli app --port 7801 midi.new_clip '{"track":"Inst 1","start":"bars_beats:1|1|000","end":"bars_beats:17|1|000"}'
```

Once a clip exists, selecting it with the Grabber and drawing in the MIDI Editor works fine.

title: soundcraft-ui-egui tests fail now and then when run in parallel (shared palette flag)
author: iannitram
body:
On `main` (`6cf896e`), `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui --lib` failed 2 runs out of 40 for me, and 0 out of 10 with `--test-threads=1`. That was Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2, 24 threads, Rust 1.99.0. Rust 1.95 shows the same two tests failing at about the same rate, including inside `cargo xtask ci`, so a gate run can go red on a change that never touched the UI.

Two tests fail, one or both in a run:

```
thread 'theme::tests::application_frames_follow_system_appearance_and_preserve_manual_palettes' panicked at crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs:472:17:
assertion `left == right` failed: custom palette for System with Some(Light)
  left: false
 right: true
```

```
thread 'edit_window::tests::shift_click_adds_another_track_to_the_selection' panicked at crates/ui-egui/src/edit_window.rs:2287:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: [2, 3]
 right: [0, 2, 3]
```

**Likely cause** (from reading the code; I have not confirmed it with a fix): `theme::LIGHT_THEME` is one flag for the whole process, and `theme::apply` stores it. `lock_test_palette()` is there to stop tests changing it under each other, but only tests in `theme.rs` and `widgets.rs` take it. The `edit_window` harness tests also run whole frames, and they find painted rows by colour: `highlighted_rows` matches `Tokens::current().selection`. They don't take the lock. So the theme test can switch the palette to light between an `edit_window` test painting its rows and looking them up (a row goes missing, as above), and another test's frame can put the palette back to dark between the theme test's `apply` and its `is_light()` assertion.

**To reproduce:**

```sh
for i in $(seq 40); do cargo test -q -p soundcraft-ui-egui --lib >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "run $i failed"; done
```

🤖 Found and written up with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Maximizer on the master: bounce not delay-compensated (+71 samples), and ceiling is sample-peak (true peak −0.93 dBTP at −1 dB ceiling)
author: Mart95Dev
body:
## Summary

Two small issues with the Maximizer on a master fader, found while mastering a voice-over + music mix to −14 LUFS for social video (`soundcraft-cli`, headless):

1. **The bounce is delayed by the Maximizer's latency (71 samples at 48 kHz).** The plugin reports it (`fn latency` → `self.la - 1`, with `MAX_LOOKAHEAD_MS = 1.5`), but the bounced file comes out 71 samples later than the same mix without it.
2. **The ceiling is a sample-peak ceiling, so the true peak ends up above it.** With `ceiling: -1`, the bounce reports `peak_db: -1.00` but `true_peak_db: -0.93`. Most delivery specs (−1 dBTP for streaming and social platforms) are written in true peak, so the ceiling doesn't guarantee compliance.

## Reproduction

Session at 48 kHz: a mono voice track imported at 2 s (44.1 kHz source, resampled on import) and a stereo music track, with EQ/compressor/de-esser on the voice and volume automation on the music. Then, on top of that session:

```
# A: no master insert
soundcraft-cli run --in mix.scraft \
  --cmd 'file.bounce_mix={"path":"a.wav","format":"wav","bit_depth":24,"start":{"seconds":0},"end":{"seconds":30}}'

# B: master fader + Gain (0 latency)
soundcraft-cli run --in mix.scraft --cmd 'track.new={"kind":"master","format":"stereo"}' \
  --cmd 'mix.insert={"track":7,"slot":0,"plugin":"gain","params":{}}' \
  --cmd 'file.bounce_mix={"path":"b.wav", … same …}'

# C: master fader + Maximizer
soundcraft-cli run --in mix.scraft --cmd 'track.new={"kind":"master","format":"stereo"}' \
  --cmd 'mix.insert={"track":7,"slot":0,"plugin":"maximizer","params":{"threshold":-7,"ceiling":-1,"release":80}}' \
  --cmd 'file.bounce_mix={"path":"c.wav", … same …}'
```

I measured the voice's position in each bounce by cross-correlating against the source, resampled to 48 kHz and expected at 2 s:

| Bounce            | Offset vs expected | Peak (reported) | True peak (reported) | True peak (independent, 4× oversampled) |
|-------------------|--------------------|-----------…

title: Sampler can't load a sample from the UI (mix.sampler_load has no menu entry), so it's silent
author: sajibsrs
body:
## Summary

The built-in **Sampler** instrument can be chosen from the app (INST label or Mix slot → **Built-in › Sampler**), but nothing in the app loads a sample into it, so it stays silent. Without a sample, Sampler makes no sound (see the module doc in `crates/dsp/src/plugins/sampler.rs`).

The engine command `mix.sampler_load` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/sampler.rs`) works, but it has no menu path or shortcut and nothing in `crates/ui-egui/src` calls it. Dropping an audio file on the track or plugin doesn't load it either. `mix.sampler_clear` is in the same state.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.6.1 (main @ 6cf896e), macOS (aarch64)

## Steps to reproduce

1. **Track › New...** → kind *Instrument*.
2. Click the **INST** label → **Built-in › Sampler**.
3. **Clip › New MIDI Clip** (#282 / #358), add notes, and press play.
4. Look for a way to load an audio file into the Sampler.

## Expected

A way to load a sample from the app, for example:
- **Load Sample...** / **Clear Sample** items in the instrument menu (`mix_window::instrument_menu`) when the instrument is Sampler, and/or in its plugin window, and/or
- dropping an audio file onto an instrument track (or its instrument slot) loads it into the Sampler.

Ideally the plugin window also shows the loaded file's name and lets you set the root note.

## Actual

There's no way to load a sample, so the Sampler is silent.

## Workaround

```sh
soundcraft-cli app --port 7801 mix.sampler_load '{"track":"Inst 1","path":"/path/to/sample.wav","params":{"root_note":60}}'
```

## Related

#282, #374. `mix.sampler_load` and `mix.sampler_clear` are listed in `KNOWN_UNREACHED` in the command reachability test added by #358.

title: midi.new_clip silently ignores clip length (`length` and `end`) when `start` is omitted
author: Sirli01
body:
## Description

`midi.new_clip` declares a `length` parameter (`{track, start?, end?|length?}`), but
when `start` is omitted, both `length` and `end` are silently ignored. The clip
falls back to the default 1-bar length, and the command reports success — no
error, no warning.

## Steps to reproduce

Via the CLI, run a script with:

session.new {"sample_rate":48000,"bit_depth":24}
event.tempo {"bpm":120}
track.new {"kind":"instrument","instrument":"sampler","name":"T"}
midi.new_clip {"track":1,"length":192000}

At 48 kHz / 120 BPM, `length:192000` (samples) should produce a 4-second
(2-bar) clip.

## Expected behavior

The returned clip spans `start:0` → `end:192000`.

## Actual behavior

The returned clip spans `start:0` → `end:96000` (exactly 1 bar = 2 seconds),
i.e. the requested length was dropped and the default applied:

midi.new_clip: {"clip":2,"end":96000,"start":0}

## Additional narrowing

The bug is specific to the omitted-`start` code path. When `start` is passed
explicitly, length works correctly:

midi.new_clip {"track":1,"length":192000}              → {"clip":2,"end":96000,"start":0}    ← length dropped
midi.new_clip {"track":1,"end":192000}                 → {"clip":7,"end":96000,"start":0}    ← end also dropped
midi.new_clip {"track":1,"start":0,"length":192000}    → {"clip":3,"end":192000,"start":0}   ← OK
midi.new_clip {"track":1,"start":0,"end":192000}       → {"clip":4,"end":192000,"start":0}   ← OK
midi.new_clip {"track":1,"start":96000,"length":192000} → {"clip":5,"end":288000,"start":96000} ← OK

So the default-start branch never consults `length` or `end`; only the
explicit-start branch does.

## Impact

This is the same failure mode as #266 (parameter silently discarded, command
reports success but the result is wrong). Any script that relies on `length`
or `end` without an explicit `start` gets a clip that's shorter than requested,
notes land outside the clip, and a subsequent bounce renders silence — with no
indication anything went wrong…

title: File › Open Recent Session
author: PiMinusMax
body:
SoundCraft has no list of recently opened sessions: every reopen goes through *Open Session...* and the file dialog. PhotoCraft, VectorCraft, FilmCraft and EffectCraft already have one.

No wasm impact: the list stays empty on the web build.

title: [Audit] Session backup destination can escape automation write roots through an existing symlink
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- soundcraft-readonly-audit:c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d:H1 -->
SoundCraft upstream audit 2026-10-13 — finding **H1**.

**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High.
**Status:** Source-confirmed control flow/contract issue; not runtime-reproduced. Reviewed upstream [`c0cb993`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/commit/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d), rechecked as main before filing. Rust tooling was unavailable; no build, crafted-file execution, destructive test, or exploit was run.

### Source evidence and root cause
- [`crates/engine/src/io.rs:1021-1040`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L1021-L1040)

`back_up` checks `check_write(&backups)` for the directory, but not the destination passed to `std::fs::copy`. The backup number uses `n.saturating_add(1)`, so exhaustion reuses the existing highest-numbered destination.

### Conditions
A permitted project directory already contains a maximum-numbered backup symlink to a writable file outside the automation write root. Saving changed session contents can follow that destination. No concurrent filesystem mutation is required.

### Impact
Overwrites a file outside the configured write authority. This is conditional on pre-existing project contents and process filesystem permissions; it is not a remote-network claim.

### Recommended remediation
Validate the actual destination, reject counter exhaustion, and exclusively create backups without following existing destination entries.

### Suggested regression coverage (not executed)
In disposable test directories, use a maximum-numbered backup symlink to an outside sentinel and assert saving leaves the sentinel unchanged. Also test ordinary counter exhaustion.

title: [Audit] Video pixel budgets are enforced after ProRes allocation and not on H.264 coded geometry
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- soundcraft-readonly-audit:c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d:H2 -->
SoundCraft upstream audit 2026-10-13 — finding **H2**.

**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High.
**Status:** Source-confirmed control flow/contract issue; not runtime-reproduced. Reviewed upstream [`c0cb993`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/commit/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d), rechecked as main before filing. Rust tooling was unavailable; no build, crafted-file execution, destructive test, or exploit was run.

### Source evidence and root cause
- [`crates/video/src/prores/decode.rs:175-185`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d/crates/video/src/prores/decode.rs#L175-L185)
- [`crates/video/src/movie.rs:397-401`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d/crates/video/src/movie.rs#L397-L401)
- [`crates/video/src/movie.rs:425-428`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d/crates/video/src/movie.rs#L425-L428)
- [`crates/video/src/h264/params.rs:395-398`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d/crates/video/src/h264/params.rs#L395-L398)

ProRes resizes image planes before Movie checks `MAX_PIXELS`. H.264 accepts SPS dimensions up to 1024 macroblocks per dimension; decoded geometry is not subjected to the Movie pixel budget before picture allocation or RGBA conversion. The earlier container-dimension check is not a check of the coded dimensions.

### Conditions
Codec dimensions exceed the budget even though container metadata passes the opening check.

### Impact
Potential multi-gigabyte allocations, long stalls, or allocation-failure termination while opening/decoding media. Source establishes the missing preallocation guard, not an executed crash.

### Recommended remediation
Validate coded geometry and an aggregate decoder-memory budget before allocating planes, reference frames, macroblock…

Total latency uses the maximum individual aux latency (`lmax_a`), but every aux stage inserts alignment toward that maximum. An audio -> delayed aux -> zero-latency aux -> main chain therefore accumulates more physical delay than reported.

### Conditions and realistic impact

Compute cumulative path latency and compensate at summing points, including the selected bounce output.

Test two/three aux stages, direct parallel routes, main and named-bus outputs, partial intervals, and different block sizes.

Preserve/deliver pending releases or perform a processor reset that actually clears voices before forgetting them.

- [`xtask/src/version.rs:105-116`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d/xtask/src/version.rs#L105-L116)

The validator permits zero-prefixed numeric prerelease identifiers and does not fully validate numeric bounds. run replaces the manifest before Cargo validates it; subsequent cargo_update failure does not restore the old file.

### Conditions and realistic impact
A version such as a numeric prerelease with a leading zero passes the local validator but Cargo rejects it, leaving the workspace manifest unusable until manually repaired.

### Recommended remediation
Use complete SemVer validation before replacement and preserve/restore the original manifest on update failure.

### Suggested regression coverage (not executed)
Test invalid numeric prereleases, numeric overflow and simulated cargo-update failure; rejected updates must preserve the original manifest.

title: [Audit] MIDI writer masks out-of-range pitch and controller identifiers instead of clamping
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- soundcraft-readonly-audit:c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d:L10 -->
SoundCraft upstream audit 2026-10-13 — finding **L10**.

**Severity:** Low (narrow exposure or public-library/malformed-input edge case). **Confidence:** High in source behavior.
**Status:** Source review, not runtime-reproduced. Audited upstream [`c0cb993`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/commit/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d), rechecked as main before filing. Cargo/rustc were unavailable; no build, destructive test, or exploit was run.

### Source evidence and root cause

Several values use `& 0x7F` (pitch, release velocity, controller identifiers), while the writer documentation promises clamping and note-on velocity already clamps.

### Conditions and realistic impact
Public model values of 128 or 255 wrap into different notes/controllers rather than being rejected/clamped. Normal sanitized callers may not supply them; the public serialization contract still differs.

### Recommended remediation
Validate or clamp consistently at the writer boundary and clarify policy for invalid controller identities.

### Suggested regression coverage (not executed)
Test 127, 128 and 255 and independently inspect the resulting event values.

title: [Audit] Signed Exp-Golomb decoder wraps an unrepresentable positive result into i32
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- soundcraft-readonly-audit:c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d:L11 -->
SoundCraft upstream audit 2026-10-13 — finding **L11**.

**Severity:** Low (narrow exposure or public-library/malformed-input edge case). **Confidence:** High in source behavior.
**Status:** Source review, not runtime-reproduced. Audited upstream [`c0cb993`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/commit/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d), rechecked as main before filing. Cargo/rustc were unavailable; no build, destructive test, or exploit was run.

### Source evidence and root cause

`read_se` maps an odd unsigned code to `(k + 1) / 2`, then casts that i64 value to i32 without range validation.

### Conditions and realistic impact
The largest odd unsigned code maps beyond i32::MAX and becomes negative. Invalid input is accepted with the wrong signed value rather than rejected.

### Recommended remediation
Use checked conversion and report an invalid code when the signed result is not representable.

### Suggested regression coverage (not executed)
Test both signed representable boundaries and the first out-of-range positive mapping.

title: [Audit investigation] Investigate Audio Unit input-buffer aliasing after a previously lent buffer is reused
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- soundcraft-readonly-audit:c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d:P1 -->
SoundCraft upstream audit 2026-10-13 — investigation **P1**.

**Potential severity:** High if reachable. **Confidence:** Medium; real-AU reachability not established.
**Status: Investigation required, not a confirmed end-to-end vulnerability.** Audited upstream [`c0cb993`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/commit/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d), rechecked as main before filing. No runtime reproduction, exploit, destructive test, or sanitizer run was performed. Cargo/rustc were unavailable.

### Established source evidence
- [`crates/au-host/src/ffi.rs:482-503`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d/crates/au-host/src/ffi.rs#L482-L503)

The callback obtains mutable access to an input buffer and can lend its pointer when b.data is null. For a subsequent non-null b.data it creates a mutable destination slice, then reads the source while writing the destination, without an overlap check.

### Conditions and unresolved premise
If an AU returns the previously lent source pointer as the next destination, the references overlap. That pointer configuration is problematic for Rust aliasing; whether a compliant AU supplies it is not established here. Repeated callbacks alone do not prove the configuration occurs.

### Conditional impact
Potential undefined behavior if the overlapping-buffer case is allowed/reachable. This is not a demonstrated memory-safety vulnerability.

### Recommended remediation / decision
Confirm the callback contract. Avoid constructing overlapping Rust references; explicitly distinguish already-lent host buffers or use a validated overlap-safe copying/storage strategy.

### Suggested verification and regression coverage (not executed)
Build a callback-level test for null-buffer lending followed by reuse of that exact pointer, ideally under Miri, and validate reachability against compliant Audio Units.

title: [Audit investigation] Investigate callback-context lifetime when Audio Unit disposal returns an error
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- soundcraft-readonly-audit:c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d:P2 -->
SoundCraft upstream audit 2026-10-13 — investigation **P2**.

**Potential severity:** High if disposal can leave callbacks live. **Confidence:** Medium; disposal failure contract unresolved.
**Status: Investigation required, not a confirmed end-to-end vulnerability.** Audited upstream [`c0cb993`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/commit/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d), rechecked as main before filing. No runtime reproduction, exploit, destructive test, or sanitizer run was performed. Cargo/rustc were unavailable.

### Established source evidence
- [`crates/au-host/src/ffi.rs:944-957`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/c0cb99340891d306e216582db465f3594b89dc1d/crates/au-host/src/ffi.rs#L944-L957)

Instance::drop ignores AudioUnitUninitialize and AudioComponentInstanceDispose return statuses, then unconditionally frees the input and host-time callback contexts.

### Conditions and unresolved premise
A disposal call fails. A dangling callback context follows only if that failure can leave the unit alive/capable of callbacks; the source alone does not establish that external contract.

### Conditional impact
Potential use-after-free under that failure semantics. Not a reproduced UAF and not a claim that every nonzero disposal status leaves a live unit.

### Recommended remediation / decision
Establish disposal/quiescence guarantees. If failure can leave the instance alive, retain the entire callback backing storage rather than free it until safe teardown is guaranteed.

### Suggested verification and regression coverage (not executed)
Add disposal-failure injection and verify backing-context lifetime, paired with authoritative platform-contract validation.

title: macOS: CLAP plugins with only an embedded editor (e.g. FabFilter) can't open their GUI
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
## Summary

On macOS, a CLAP plugin that offers only an embedded editor can't show its own GUI. **Open Plugin Editor** does nothing visible; the status line (Edit window only) says:

> Pro-Q 4: this plugin offers only an embedded editor, which SoundCraft hosts on Windows only

Many CLAP plugins only offer an embedded editor (`clap.gui` with `is_floating = false`), so on macOS they can only be used through the generic parameter sliders. VST3 editors work on macOS, so the same plugin works as VST3 but not as CLAP.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.6.1 (main @ c0cb993), macOS (aarch64)
- FabFilter Pro-Q 4 / Pro-Q 3 / Pro-L 2 / Pro-MB (CLAP)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add **CLAP › FabFilter › Pro-Q 4** to an insert slot.
2. Open the plugin window and click **Open Plugin Editor**.
3. Switch to the Edit window and read the status line.

## Expected

The plugin's own editor opens in a host window, as it does on Windows and as VST3 editors do on macOS.

## Actual

Nothing opens. The status line shows the message above.

## Notes

- `crates/clap-host/src/ffi.rs`: `GuiLink::open` falls back to `open_embedded` only when `hostwin::SUPPORTED`. The `hostwin` module exists for Windows only (#315); every other platform gets the stub with `SUPPORTED = false`.
- `crates/vst3-host/src/ffi.rs` already has a macOS host window (`mod window`: an `NSWindow` whose content `NSView` the plugin view attaches to, with resizing). A macOS `hostwin` for CLAP could follow it and pass the content view as `clap_window_handle.cocoa`.
- Related, smaller: when this happens in the Mix window the error is invisible, since the status line is only drawn in the Edit window.

title: Inserting a plugin should open it, without an extra click
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
## Summary

Choosing a plugin for an empty insert slot adds it but doesn't open it, so every new plugin takes an extra click on its slot before you can set it up. DAWs generally open a plugin as soon as you insert it (Pro Tools, Logic and Ableton all do), because the next thing you want is almost always to adjust it.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.6.1 (main @ c0cb993), macOS (aarch64), demo session

## Steps to reproduce

1. In the Mix window (or the Edit window's Inserts column), click an empty insert slot.
2. Choose a plugin, e.g. **EQ › EQ 7-Band**, or a CLAP/VST3 plugin.

## Expected

The plugin opens straight away with its own GUI. In Pro Tools, as in every other DAW, inserting a plugin opens it with its own GUI, so a third-party plugin should open its own editor, not the generic parameter window. Replacing the plugin in a filled slot should open the new one the same way, since it's a new plugin to set up.

Where a plugin's own editor can't open yet (CLAP plugins with only an embedded editor on macOS, #485), SoundCraft's plugin window should open instead, so something still opens.

## Actual

The plugin is inserted and the menu closes. Nothing opens until you click the slot.

## Notes

- `crates/ui-egui/src/mix_window.rs`: `plugin_menu` runs `mix.insert` through `run_pick`, which only runs the command and closes the menu. Clicking a filled slot pushes `(track, slot)` to `app.ui.plugin_windows` (`insert_slot`). The Edit window's Inserts column uses the same `insert_slot` (#377), so one change covers both.
- The window should open from the menu pick in the UI, not from `mix.insert` itself: programmatic calls (CLI, MCP, control channel) shouldn't open windows.

title: Automation breakpoints can't be grabbed and dragged to adjust them
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
## Summary

Existing automation breakpoints can't be adjusted. In an automation view (volume, pan, plugin parameters…) only the Pencil does anything: a click adds a breakpoint and a drag draws a new curve. To change a point that's already there, you have to draw over it.

DAWs generally let you grab breakpoints and drag them (Pro Tools, Logic and Ableton all do), which is how you ride a fader move after the fact. For example, in Pro Tools, with the Grabber (or the Smart Tool) in an automation view:

- drag a breakpoint up or down to change its value, and sideways to move it in time;
- click on the line to add a breakpoint;
- Alt-click a breakpoint to delete it;
- select several breakpoints and drag them together.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.6.1 (main @ c0cb993), macOS (aarch64), demo session

## Steps to reproduce

1. Show a track's volume automation and add a few breakpoints with the Pencil.
2. Choose the Grabber and drag one of the breakpoints up.

## Expected

The breakpoint follows the pointer, and the move is one undo step.

## Actual

Nothing happens. The Grabber only acts on clips.

## Notes

- `crates/ui-egui/src/edit_window.rs`: in the track lane's gesture handling, `Tool::Grabber` only starts `Gesture::MoveClips` on a clip hit, and only `Tool::Pencil` uses `auto_view`.
- The engine has `automation.set_point` but no command to move or delete a single breakpoint (`set_point`, `write_range`, `clear`, `thin`, …), so this probably needs one, so that a drag works through the same command path as everything else and is one undo step (like `execute_merged` for clip gain).

title: Undo should cover edits, not listening and view controls
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
## Summary

Cmd+Z undoes things that aren't edits: Solo, Mute, Record Enable, track height and view, group activation and more. Soloing a track to listen, then pressing Cmd+Z to undo the last edit, undoes the solo instead, and every solo, mute or record-arm press fills the undo history.

In Pro Tools, Logic Pro and Ableton Live, undo is for edits. Listening, recording and view controls aren't undo steps. SoundCraft already keeps zoom out of undo the same way (`view` commands).

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.6.1 (main @ c0cb993), macOS (aarch64), demo session

## Steps to reproduce

1. Move or trim a clip.
2. Solo, mute or record-enable a track, or change its height.
3. Press Cmd+Z.

## Expected

The clip edit is undone, and the solo, mute, record enable or track height stays as it is.

## Actual

The solo, mute, record enable or height change is undone. A second Cmd+Z undoes the clip edit.

## Commands that shouldn't be undo steps

Currently plain (undoable) `cmd!` specs:

- **Listening and recording:** `mix.solo`, `mix.mute`, `mix.solo_safe`, `mix.clear_solos`, `mix.clear_mutes`, `mix.record_arm`, `mix.input_monitor`, `track.set_record_to_input_only`
- **View:** `track.height`, `track.height_up`, `track.height_down`, `track.view`, `track.hide`, `track.change_width`
- **State:** `track.group_toggle`, `mix.automation_mode`, `mix.insert_bypass`, `track.bypass_*` (Bypass Inserts)

`track.pin` and `track.color` stay undoable, as in Pro Tools.

## Notes

- Marking these `noundo` alone isn't enough. Undo restores a whole-document snapshot (`Engine::undo` in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`), so the next Cmd+Z would silently restore the solo, mute, arm, height and so on from before the edit. Undo and redo should carry the current state of these settings over to the restored document, as `keep_edit_mode` already does for the edit mode.
- The session is still marked modified when they change, since they're saved with it.
- `track.clear_clip_indicators` and `event.all_notes_off` a…

title: New Session can't start from a template saved with Save As Template
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
## Summary

**File › Save As Template...** saves a session's tracks, routing, plugins and sends without its audio, but nothing can use the result: **File › New...** offers only a blank session or the demo. To start from your own template you have to open the template file and immediately Save As, and risk overwriting the template if you forget.

DAWs let you start a new session from a template: in Pro Tools, the Dashboard's **Create from Template** lists your templates (and the built-in ones) by group; Logic and Ableton have the same idea. A mixing or mastering setup is exactly what people keep as a template.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.6.1 (main @ c0cb993), macOS (aarch64)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set up a session (tracks, buses, inserts, sends) and choose **File › Save As Template...**.
2. Choose **File › New...**.

## Expected

The New Session dialog lists your templates, and choosing one creates a new, untitled session from it (the template file itself is left unchanged).

## Actual

The dialog offers only "Start from the demo session". There's no way to choose a template.

## Notes

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`: `session.new` takes `template?: blank|demo` only. `session.save_template` writes a `.scraft` (clips, sources and video removed) to any path the user picks, so SoundCraft doesn't know where templates are.
- A templates folder (per user, like Pro Tools' Session Templates folder) would let Save As Template save there by default and New Session list what's in it, while `session.new` could take a template path, e.g. `template?: blank|demo|<path>`.
- Part of G-16 in `docs/gaps.md` (session templates, track presets, workspace browser).

title: macOS: Audio Unit plugins can't open their own editor
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
## Summary

Audio Unit plugins insert and play, but their own GUI can't be opened: **Open Plugin Editor** is greyed out ("This plugin has no editor of its own, or it is not loaded"), so an AU can only be used through SoundCraft's generic parameter sliders.

Audio Units are the native plugin format on macOS (the one Logic uses), and most vendors ship their plugins as AU. In every DAW that hosts AU, inserting one shows its own GUI. Without it, EQs, compressors and channel strips that are designed to be used through their interface are hard to use at all.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.6.1 (main @ c0cb993), macOS (aarch64)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add any plugin from **Audio Units** in an insert slot's menu.
2. Open the plugin window.

## Expected

**Open Plugin Editor** opens the plugin's own GUI in a host window, as it does for VST3 plugins on macOS.

## Actual

The button is greyed out and only the generic parameter sliders are shown.

## Notes

- `crates/au-host/src/lib.rs`: "Not hosted yet: Audio Unit editor views (Cocoa `AUCocoaUIBase`)". The AU host has no editor, so the default `editor()` returns none. `docs/plugin-parity.md` lists "Editors: AU ❌ — Cocoa view hosting missing".
- `crates/vst3-host/src/ffi.rs` already has a macOS host window (`mod window`: an `NSWindow` whose content `NSView` the plugin view attaches to, with resizing). An AU editor could reuse the same approach: get the unit's Cocoa view (`kAudioUnitProperty_CocoaUI` → `AUCocoaUIBase uiViewForAudioUnit:withSize:`) and put it in such a window.
- Related: #485 (CLAP plugins with only an embedded editor on macOS) needs the same kind of host window.

title: Sidechain (key input) for compressors and other dynamics plugins
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
## Summary

There's no sidechain in SoundCraft: a plugin can only react to its own track's signal. Keyed compression (bass ducking under the kick, a vocal pushing down a music bed), keyed gates and de-essing from another source can't be set up, with either the built-in dynamics or third-party plugins.

Every DAW used for mixing has this. In Pro Tools it's called **Key Input** and uses buses:

1. On the source (e.g. the kick), add a send to a bus, e.g. Bus 1 (often pre-fader, so the key doesn't follow the kick's fader).
2. On the target (e.g. the bass), insert a compressor.
3. In the plugin window, choose **Bus 1** in the key input menu (the key icon).
4. Turn on **External Key**, so the compressor reacts to the bus instead of its own signal.
5. **Key Listen** lets you hear the key signal, and the built-in dynamics have a key filter (HPF/LPF), e.g. to react only to the kick's low end.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.6.1 (main @ c0cb993), macOS (aarch64)

## Expected

A plugin window has a key input menu listing the session's buses, plus External Key and Key Listen, for the built-in Compressor, Expander/Gate and De-Esser, and for third-party plugins that have a sidechain input.

## Actual

No key input anywhere. Third-party plugins' sidechain inputs are left inactive.

## Notes

- `crates/dsp/src/lib.rs`: `Plugin::process(&mut self, io, frames)` takes one buffer, the track's own signal, so built-in plugins have nowhere to receive a key. `compressor`'s "sidechain high-pass" (`crates/dsp/src/plugins/dynamics.rs`) filters its own signal.
- Hosts: `crates/vst3-host/src/lib.rs` keeps aux (sidechain) buses inactive; `crates/au-host/src/lib.rs` hosts no extra buses; `crates/clap-host` uses only the main audio port.
- The mix engine would need to render the key bus before the track whose insert listens to it, and handle the extra latency in delay compensation.
- `docs/plugin-parity.md` lists "Sidechain / key input ❌ — All three hosts" (part of G-13 in `docs/gaps.md`).

title: Bounce: dither can't be turned off (always on for 16/24-bit)
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
## Summary

Every 16- and 24-bit bounce is dithered (TPDF ±1 LSB), and there's no way to turn it off from the Bounce dialog. `file.bounce_stems` always dithers, even when called with parameters.

When mastering, dither is applied once, as the very last step, usually by the master limiter (many have their own dither) or a dither plugin on the master. A bounce that adds its own dither on top dithers the master twice. In Pro Tools, a bounce isn't dithered unless you put a dither plugin on the master yourself.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.6.1 (main @ c0cb993), macOS (aarch64)

## Steps to reproduce

1. **File › Bounce Mix...** with Bit Depth 16-bit or 24-bit.
2. Look for a dither option.

## Expected

A **Dither** checkbox in the Bounce dialog, so a bounce can be written without dither. Off by default, as in Pro Tools, since the master chain decides.

## Actual

No option. The bounce is always dithered (32-bit float is the only way to avoid it).

## Notes

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`: `file.bounce_mix` takes `dither?: true`, but the Bounce dialog (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`, `Dialog::Bounce`) never sends it, so it's always the default.
- `file.bounce_stems` hard-codes `dither: true` in its `EncodeOptions`; it should take the same `dither` parameter.
- Dither is implemented in `crates/audio-io/src/pcm.rs` (`Quantizer`, TPDF).

title: Recording engine applies an identical ~14.4kHz bandwidth-limiting artifact regardless of input device
author: B-Rietz
body:
## Summary

Audio recorded through SoundCraft's engine sounds noticeably degraded/processed compared to the same physical microphone recorded in another DAW (Adobe Audition) with identical system-level audio settings — and the degradation is *identical* regardless of which input device is selected, which points at something in the recording/monitoring signal path rather than the device driver or OS.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.6.1 (macOS universal build, both CLI and app)
- macOS 15.6.1 (Sequoia), Apple Silicon
- Input device: a USB condenser mic/interface ("ME6S"), 48kHz / 24-bit, buffer size 64 samples
- Control channel used for setup/routing: `soundcraft-cli app --port <port> ...`

## What I did

1. Recorded a short VO take on an armed mono track with input routed to the USB mic (`track.input` → the mic's bus, confirmed via `session.inspect`).
2. Playback sounded noticeably different/worse than expected for a dedicated USB mic — thin, processed, more like a laptop's built-in mic.
3. To isolate the cause, ran an A/B test: recorded the same short phrase twice, once with `setup.hardware`/`track.input` pointed at the MacBook's built-in mic, once pointed at the USB mic — two different tracks, two different physical devices, same session/buffer/bit-depth settings.
4. Compared the two resulting WAV files with `ffmpeg`'s `showspectrumpic` filter.

## What I found

**Both recordings show the identical artifact**: a hard, near-brickwall frequency ceiling at ~14.4kHz, with narrow broadband noise bursts persisting above that line even during silence. Two physically different microphones should not share an identical, razor-sharp frequency ceiling at the same frequency — that's the signature of a shared *software* processing/filtering stage applied after capture, not the natural frequency response of either mic.

To rule out macOS itself (e.g. system Microphone Mode / Voice Isolation), I recorded the same USB mic, same system-level audio settings, directly in Adobe Auditi…

title: convert: TPDF dither is always applied, so digital silence and same-depth conversions are altered
author: Tokarzewski
body:
**Version:** SoundCraft CLI 0.6.1 (release build). The same code is on main at c0cb993 (`apps/soundcraft-cli/src/main.rs`, `EncodeOptions { ..., dither: true, ... }` in `convert`); I built it and got identical numbers.

`soundcraft-cli convert` has no dither option and always dithers (TPDF, about 1 LSB) whatever the source and target depth. A conversion that does not reduce resolution therefore still changes the audio, and digital silence turns into noise.

## Steps

```python
# make.py: 0.1 s of 16-bit mono digital silence, and a 16-bit sine
import wave, struct, math
def put(name, samples):
    with wave.open(name, "wb") as w:
        w.setnchannels(1); w.setsampwidth(2); w.setframerate(48000)
        w.writeframes(struct.pack("<%dh" % len(samples), *samples))
put("silence.wav", [0] * 4800)
put("tone.wav", [int(8000 * math.sin(i * 0.05)) for i in range(4800)])
```

```sh
soundcraft-cli convert silence.wav silence16.wav --bit-depth 16   # exit 0
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav tone16.wav --bit-depth 16         # exit 0
```

```python
import wave, struct
def samples(name):
    with wave.open(name) as w: return struct.unpack("<%dh" % w.getnframes(), w.readframes(w.getnframes()))
s = samples("silence16.wav")
print(sum(1 for x in s if x), "of", len(s), "samples are non-zero, max", max(map(abs, s)))
a, b = samples("tone.wav"), samples("tone16.wav")
print(sum(1 for x, y in zip(a, b) if x != y), "of", len(a), "samples changed")
```

## Observed

- Silence: 1199 of 4800 samples are non-zero (values of +/-1 LSB).
- 16-bit to 16-bit: 1199 of 4800 samples differ from the source by 1 LSB.
- Converting 16-bit to the default 24-bit output also changes samples (a 16-bit file is already exactly representable in 24-bit, so nothing needs dithering).
- The dither sequence is deterministic, so the result is repeatable but not transparent.

## Expected

A conversion that does not reduce resolution (same depth, 16 to 24, anything to 32f) should copy the samples exactly, and digital silen…

title: convert, run: unknown, misspelled or value-less options are silently ignored (exit 0)
author: Tokarzewski
body:
**Version:** SoundCraft CLI 0.6.1 (release build); also on main at c0cb993 (checked by building it). The cases below are ones that main's #256 fix does not reject.

`convert` and `run` look options up with `arg_value(args, "--flag")` and never check what is left over. A misspelled option, an `--option=value` form or an option with its value missing is treated as absent, so the command succeeds and does something other than what was asked.

## Steps

```python
import wave
with wave.open("tone.wav", "wb") as w:
    w.setnchannels(1); w.setsampwidth(2); w.setframerate(48000); w.writeframes(b"\x00\x10" * 4800)
```

```sh
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav out.wav --rate                 # no value
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav out.wav --rate=44100
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav out.wav --bitdepth 16
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav out.wav --bit-depth=16
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav out.wav --normalise            # UK spelling of --normalize
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav out.wav --bogus
soundcraft-cli run --cmd session.new --bounce                  # no path
soundcraft-cli run --cmd session.new --bounces x.wav
soundcraft-cli run --cmd session.new --bounce=y.wav
echo $?
```

## Observed

Every command exits 0 with nothing on stderr.

- The six `convert` variants each write `out.wav` at 48000 Hz, 24-bit, un-normalised (`soundcraft-cli info out.wav`), i.e. the requested rate, depth or normalisation is silently not applied.
- The three `run` commands print `session.new: ...` and exit 0, but no bounce file is written.

## Expected

An unknown option, or a known option without its value, should be reported (for example `unknown option --bitdepth`, `--rate needs a value`) with a non-zero exit, as `--rate 4410x` already is on main. Accepting `--opt=value` would be a bonus.

## Related issues

- #256 (closed): invalid `--rate` / `--bit-depth` values. Missing values and unknown options are still unchecked.
- #96 (closed): `--bounce` / `--save` reporting success without produci…

title: Damaged or truncated FLAC decodes to shorter audio with exit 0 (corrupt frames are skipped and later audio shifts earlier)
author: Tokarzewski
body:
**Version:** SoundCraft CLI 0.6.1 (release build); the decoder is unchanged on main at c0cb993 (built and checked).

When a FLAC file has a corrupt frame, the decoder drops that frame and carries on, and when the file is cut short it simply stops. `convert` and `file.import_audio` report success, print nothing on stderr, and produce shorter audio. For a corrupt frame in the middle, everything after it moves earlier by one block, so the result is out of sync with any other stem that is not damaged. `info` reports the length from the header, so it disagrees with what is actually decoded.

## Steps

```python
# make.py
import wave, struct, math
with wave.open("long.wav", "wb") as w:
    w.setnchannels(1); w.setsampwidth(2); w.setframerate(48000)
    w.writeframes(struct.pack("<48000h", *[int(8000 * math.sin(i * 0.05)) for i in range(48000)]))
```

```sh
soundcraft-cli convert long.wav long.flac
python -c "
b = bytearray(open('long.flac','rb').read())
open('cut.flac','wb').write(bytes(b[:len(b)//2]))   # first half only
b[len(b)//2] ^= 0xFF                                # flip one byte in the middle
open('damaged.flac','wb').write(b)"
soundcraft-cli info damaged.flac
soundcraft-cli convert damaged.flac damaged.wav --bit-depth 16; echo "exit $?"
soundcraft-cli info damaged.wav
soundcraft-cli convert cut.flac cut.wav --bit-depth 16; echo "exit $?"
soundcraft-cli info cut.wav
```

## Observed

- `info damaged.flac`: `"frames": 48000`.
- `convert damaged.flac`: exit 0, stderr empty, "wrote damaged.wav (1 ch, 48000 Hz, 0.91 s)"; `info damaged.wav` shows 43904 frames, i.e. one 4096-frame block missing. Comparing with the source, the samples after the damage match the original shifted 4096 frames earlier (nothing is zero-filled).
- `convert cut.flac`: exit 0, stderr empty, 20480 frames written (the header still says 48000).
- Importing `damaged.flac` with `file.import_audio` creates a 43904-frame source with no warning.

## Expected

Damage in a lossless file should not pass …
