title: Mix window: set an input or output on all or the selected tracks at once, with cascading inputs (Option-click, as in Pro Tools)
author: Testsubject1337
body:
## What's missing

Setting up a tracking session means opening every strip's input menu in turn: the Mix window's I/O menu sets exactly one track, and there is no way to put one input on many tracks or to spread an interface's channels over them. Pro Tools does this from the same menu with modifiers, and it's one of the first things an engineer reaches for after Track › New:

- **Option-click** an input or output: every track gets it.
- **Option+Shift-click**: the selected tracks get it.
- **Option+Command-click** (and with Shift, on the selected tracks): the inputs **cascade**: the clicked track gets the chosen input, the next track the next channel(s), a stereo track taking two (`In 3`, `In 4-5`, `In 6`, …).

Today `route_menu` in `crates/ui-egui/src/mix_window.rs` sends one `track.input` per click with a single track, with no modifier handling, and the hardware inputs are the fixed names `In 1`…`In 8`.

## Related, larger: no input paths in I/O Setup

Setup › I/O lists busses and output paths only; `setup.io` has `create_output` but no input paths, and there is no channel matrix (`docs/ui-parity.md`: "I/O Setup 🟡: Busses and paths; no hardware channel matrix (G-01)"). Users can't name an interface's channels or pick which physical channel a track records (#336, #42). That part belongs with G-01 (duplex stream, per-channel I/O mapping) and is not covered by the PR below, but the bulk assignment should carry over once input paths exist, since it works on path names.

## Proposal

1. The Mix window's I/O menus read the modifiers on the click (Alt = all tracks, Alt+Shift = selected, with Cmd/Ctrl = cascade) and send one `track.input` / `track.output` with `tracks: [...]`, so it's one undo step. A hint line in the menu says what the modifiers do.
2. `track.input` gets `cascade: true`: given `In N`, it assigns `In N`, then the channels after it track by track, so the CLI, control channel and MCP can do the same. Refused for a bus, "none" or an output, before anything c…

title: Autosave test fails when the temp dir is on tmpfs (saved file and autosave share one mtime)
author: tydude001
body:
`autosave::tests::unsaved_work_is_offered_once_its_session_closes` (`crates/engine/src/autosave.rs`) fails every
time when the temp dir is on tmpfs, and passes with it on btrfs:

```
index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0
```

Fedora mounts `/tmp` as tmpfs by default, so `cargo xtask ci` fails there on `main` (`3a28a657`).

`leftovers()` offers an autosave only when its session file is strictly newer than the file it came from
(`saved > o`, line 274), and otherwise discards the folder as outdated. The test saves `Song.scraft` and writes
the autosave moments later. With `eprintln!`s added to `leftovers()`, the tmpfs run shows both files
with the same mtime, so the folder is discarded and `left` is empty:

```
origin_saved=Some(SystemTime { tv_sec: 1792000006, tv_nsec: 24247414 })
saved=Ok(SystemTime { tv_sec: 1792000006, tv_nsec: 24247414 })
```

I haven't pinned down why the two writes collide on tmpfs and not on btrfs: a standalone probe writing two files
back to back got distinct mtimes on both. I don't see a user-facing problem, since real autosaves live under the
config dir, not the temp dir. So it's the test that needs the two writes apart, for example by moving
`Song.scraft`'s mtime back a second before `leftovers()` runs.

Kernel 7.2.9 (Fedora 44 toolbox), `/tmp` tmpfs.

title: Complete Grid and Nudge time scales, increments, and timeline rendering
author: SlyLaM
body:
## Problem

The Grid and Nudge controls currently support only a subset of the time scales and increments needed.

This limits editing workflows that depend on musical values, timecode frames, feet and frames, samples, or clip and marker boundaries.

## Proposed behavior

Complete the Grid and Nudge selectors so they cover all the possibilities.

### Minutes:Seconds

- 1 second
- 500 ms
- 100 ms
- 10 ms
- 1 ms

### Timecode

- 1 second
- 5 frames
- 1 frame
- 1/2 frame
- 1/4 frame
- 1 subframe

The values must use the session timecode frame rate.

### Bars|Beats

- 1 bar
- Whole note
- Half note
- Quarter note
- Eighth note
- Sixteenth note
- Thirty-second note
- Sixty-fourth note
- Dotted modifier
- Triplet modifier

Musical grid positions must follow the session tempo and meter maps.

### Feet+Frames

- 1 foot
- 1 frame
- 1/4 frame
- 1 subframe

### Samples

- 10000 samples
- 1000 samples
- 100 samples
- 10 samples
- 2 samples
- 1 sample

Sample-based positions must use the session sample rate.

### Clips/Markers

Grid should also support a Clips/Markers mode based on clip boundaries and marker positions.

This mode is available for Grid only. It must not appear in the Nudge selector.

### Time scale selection

Both selectors should allow the following time scales:

- Bars|Beats
- Min:Secs
- Timecode
- Feet+Frames
- Samples

Grid additionally supports:

- Clips/Markers

Both selectors should provide a **Follow Main Time Scale** option.

## Grid behavior

When Grid edit mode is active, the Edit timeline must render grid lines matching the selected Grid time scale and increment.

title: Drag an insert to move it, Option-drag to copy it to another slot or track
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
## Summary

There's no quick way to put a plugin you've already set up on another track, or to reorder the inserts on a track. Insert slots only respond to clicks (open, Cmd-click to bypass, right-click to change), so dragging one does nothing. To reuse a plugin's settings elsewhere you have to save a user preset and load it on the other track.

DAWs generally let you drag plugins between slots and tracks. In Pro Tools:

- drag an insert to another slot, on the same track or another track, to move it;
- Option-drag (Alt on Windows) to copy it, settings included.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.7.0 (main @ 3a28a65), macOS (aarch64), demo session

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Mix window and put a plugin on a track's Insert A. Change a few of its settings.
2. Option-drag that insert onto an empty insert slot on another track.

## Expected

- A plain drag moves the insert to the slot it's dropped on, on the same track or another track.
- An Option-drag copies it there with all its settings, including the current state of a CLAP or VST3 plugin, and leaves the original in place.
- Each move or copy is one undo step.
- It works the same in the Mix window and in the Edit window's Inserts view.

Dropping onto a slot that's already in use replaces the plugin there, as in Pro Tools.

## Actual

Nothing happens. The slot doesn't start a drag.

## Notes

- `crates/ui-egui/src/mix_window.rs`: `insert_slot` senses clicks only. The Edit window's Inserts view uses the same function, so one change covers both.
- The engine has `mix.insert_move`, which swaps two slots within one track. Nothing in the UI uses it, and there's no command to copy or move an insert to another track.
- An `Insert` already carries its parameters and opaque plugin state, so copying it carries the settings. But a hosted plugin's latest state is only stored on the insert when it's captured (`capture_plugin_states`), so the source's state has to be captured before it's copied. Otherwise the copy gets the s…

title: Track presets can be saved but not recalled
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
## Summary

**Track › Save Track Preset...** saves a track's mixer, inserts, sends and instrument to a file, but nothing in the app can use the result: there's no way to recall a track preset onto a track. So a vocal chain you've set up can't be reused on another track or in another session.

DAWs let you save a track's setup and recall it later. In Pro Tools:

- **Save Track Preset** (Track menu or the track name's right-click menu) stores a track's setup in a Track Presets folder, by category. **Track Data To Recall** chooses what's included: volume, pan, I/O, inserts, sends and more.
- **Recall Track Preset** on the track name's right-click menu recalls the whole preset onto an existing track: volume, pan, inserts, sends and so on. **Recall Inserts** on an insert, or **Recall Sends** on a send, recalls only those, starting at the slot you clicked.
- The New Tracks dialog can also create tracks from a preset.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.7.0 (main @ 3a28a65), macOS (aarch64), demo session

## Steps to reproduce

1. Put a few plugins on a track (e.g. EQ and compressor on Vox) and choose **Track › Save Track Preset...**.
2. Select another track and look for a way to recall the preset.

## Expected

- **Recall Track Preset...** in the Track menu and the track name's right-click menu applies a saved preset to the selected tracks, as one undo step.
- Recalling from the track name applies the whole preset. Recalling from an insert slot applies only the inserts, starting at that slot, so a plugin chain can be reused without moving the track's fader or pan. Sends work the same way from a send slot.
- Save Track Preset saves to a Track Presets folder by default, and Recall lists the presets in it, so you choose "Vocal Chain" from a list instead of typing a path.
- A preset holds the current settings of the plugins in it, including CLAP and VST3 plugin state.

This is a significant reliability issue because users need to be able to close a project, reopen it later, and continue working without losing the original arrangement.

title: Track preset save writes stale hosted plugin state
author: euisuh
body:
Saving a track preset can serialize an earlier capture of a hosted plugin instead of its current settings. This separates the plugin-state item from #639, following the request to track those problems individually.

Reproduced on macOS arm64 at `f3a19480d8cc2d7a98cda492f5464d8c54558c9f` using the repository’s synthetic CLAP gain plugin through the real `Player` and `SoundApp::run` path; no third-party plugin or physical audio device is required by the regression.

1. Load a hosted plugin on an audio track.
2. Let its stored insert state differ from its current live state, as can happen after changing settings since the last session save/autosave.
3. Run `track.save_preset` for that track without first saving the session.
4. Inspect the preset’s insert state.

Expected: the preset contains the live hosted state at save time.

Actual: the preset contains the earlier model state. The regression sets the model to gain 0.25 while the hosted fixture has gain 1.0. It fails on unchanged production code: the saved state is `AAAAAAAA0D8AAAAAAAAAAA==`, rather than the live `AAAAAAAA8D8AAAAAAAAAAA==`.

[`SoundApp::run`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/f3a19480d8cc2d7a98cda492f5464d8c54558c9f/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L421) captures hosted states before `session.save*` and `file.bounce*`, but not before `track.save_preset`. The engine then writes the insert state already stored in the model. Reusing that capture path before preset serialization addresses this specific omission.

Scope: capture current hosted state when saving a preset through the app. Recall menus, partial insert/send recall, and preset folder browsing remain separate work under #639. The reproduction exercises CLAP; VST3 and instrument-specific runtime behavior have not been separately exercised.

title: [PR opened : #678] Improve Zoom tool feedback, zoom-out cursor, and Single Zoom mode
author: SlyLaM
body:
## Summary

The Zoom tool already supports click-and-drag zooming and modifier-click zoom-out, but its visual feedback and tool modes are incomplete.

This issue covers three related improvements:

1. Show the zoom area while dragging.
2. Display the correct zoom-out cursor when a supported modifier is held.
3. Add a Single Zoom mode that returns to the previously selected edit tool after one zoom operation.

## Current behavior

- Click-and-drag zooming works, but no visual indication shows the area being defined.
- Option-click on macOS and Alt-click on Windows/Linux zoom out correctly, but the cursor continues to display a magnifying glass with a plus sign.
- Shift+Option-click on macOS and Shift+Alt-click on Windows/Linux are not handled consistently as zoom-out gestures.
- The Zoom tool selector has no menu for choosing between persistent and single-use zooming.

## Expected behavior

### 1. Drag feedback

While dragging with the Zoom tool:

- Draw a visible zoom rectangle between the drag origin and the current pointer position.
- Update the rectangle continuously as the pointer moves.
- Make the rectangle reflect the area that will be shown after releasing the mouse.
- Clip the indicator to the editable timeline area.
- Remove it after release, cancellation with Escape, or a tool change.
- Do not create or modify the timeline selection while drawing the zoom rectangle.

### 2. Zoom-out cursor and modifiers

When the Zoom tool is active, the cursor should show:

- A magnifying glass with a plus sign for zoom-in.
- A magnifying glass with a minus sign while a zoom-out modifier is held.

| macOS | Shift+Option-click |

title: AAC/M4A import: the MP4 edit list is ignored, so the encoder delay stays in (audio starts 1024 samples late)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**SoundCraft 0.7.0 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11** (`soundcraft-cli`; main has the same symphonia 0.5.5)

AAC in MP4/M4A carries the encoder delay ("priming", usually 1024 or 2112 samples) at the start of the stream, and an edit list (`moov/trak/edts/elst`) that tells the reader which samples belong to the audio: skip `media_time` samples, then keep `segment_duration` samples. SoundCraft decodes the whole stream instead. The imported clip starts with the priming samples, so everything is late by 1024 (or 2112) samples, and it runs past the end by the padding.

**Steps**

1. Fixture `aac_priming.m4a` (13 KB), written by [`make_fixtures_soundcraft.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/soundcraft/make_fixtures_soundcraft.py) (Python standard library + ffmpeg 9.0.2's native AAC encoder): a 1.000 s, 48 kHz mono, 440 Hz tone with a single-sample click at sample 24,000. Its edit list is one entry: `media_time` 1024, `segment_duration` 48,000.
2. `soundcraft-cli info aac_priming.m4a`
3. `soundcraft-cli convert aac_priming.m4a out.wav --bit-depth 32f` (the same happens with `file.import_audio` in a session)

**Expected**: 48,000 frames (1.000 s), the click at sample 24,000 – what ffmpeg and other MP4 readers give.

**Actual** (0.7.0): `info` says `"frames": 49152, "seconds": 1.024`; the converted file has 49,152 frames and the click at sample 25,024. `file.import_audio` reports `"frames": 49152` as well.

With real-world files the offset is 1024 samples for ffmpeg-encoded AAC and 2112 samples (48 ms at 44.1 kHz) for a phone recording; a 44.1 kHz phone clip came in 2,648 frames too long. Against picture or other tracks such a clip is out of sync by 21–48 ms.

**Where**: `crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs` opens the file with `FormatOptions { enable_gapless: true, .. }`, but symphonia-format-isomp4 0.5.5 parses `edts`/`elst` (`atoms/edts.rs`) without applying it in the demuxer, so the option has no effect for MP4. Trimming `media_time` frames at the start …

body:
**SoundCraft 0.7.0 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11** (`soundcraft-cli`; main has the same symphonia 0.5.5)

AAC-LC with more than two channels can't be imported. The README lists AAC among the audio formats SoundCraft reads, and 5.1 WAV files import as six-channel tracks, but a 5.1 AAC file stops with an error. Multichannel AAC is the usual soundtrack of MP4 video exports and of web downloads.

**Steps**

1. Fixture `aac_51.m4a` (50 KB), written by [`make_fixtures_soundcraft.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/soundcraft/make_fixtures_soundcraft.py) (Python standard library + ffmpeg 9.0.2's native AAC encoder): 1.000 s, 48 kHz, 5.1 (FL FR FC LFE BL BR), a different tone on each channel.
2. `soundcraft-cli info aac_51.m4a`, or `soundcraft-cli run --cmd 'session.new={"sample_rate":48000}' --cmd 'file.import_audio={"path":"aac_51.m4a"}'`

**Expected**: a six-channel clip of 48,000 frames (the same tones as `tone_51_48k.wav`, which the generator also writes and which imports fine).

**Actual** (0.7.0): `soundcraft-cli: aac_51.m4a: unsupported audio: aac: aac too complex` (exit code 1), from `info`, `convert` and `file.import_audio` alike. All four 5.1 AAC soundtracks in our test set (MP4 and Matroska video, AAC-LC, 48 kHz) fail the same way.

**Where**: the message comes from symphonia-codec-aac 0.5.5 (`aac/mod.rs`, `AacDecoder::try_new`), which accepts only AAC-LC with at most two channels and 1024-sample frames. If a multichannel decoder isn't planned for now, an error that says what is missing ("5.1 AAC is not supported yet") would at least tell people that the file is fine.

---
*Tested and written by Claude (Anthropic). Posted for Udo Funk (@KNUFFIXX), emotional support human, who reads every report after it goes out.*

title: Import: AC-3 and E-AC-3 files are reported as "malformed audio: end of stream"
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**SoundCraft 0.7.0 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11** (`soundcraft-cli`)

AC-3 and E-AC-3 aren't among the formats SoundCraft reads, which is fine, but the message for them says the file is broken: `malformed audio: end of stream`. Other formats it doesn't decode get a clear message (an Ogg Opus file: `unsupported audio: core (codec):unsupported codec`). Someone who drops the soundtrack of a TV recording onto the timeline will think the file is damaged.

**Steps**

1. Fixtures `ac3_51.ac3` (57 KB) and `eac3_51.eac3` (49 KB), written by [`make_fixtures_soundcraft.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/soundcraft/make_fixtures_soundcraft.py) (Python standard library + ffmpeg 9.0.2's AC-3/E-AC-3 encoders): 1 s, 48 kHz, 5.1, plain elementary streams. ffprobe and ffmpeg read them.
2. `soundcraft-cli info ac3_51.ac3` (same for `eac3_51.eac3`, `convert`, or `file.import_audio` in a session)

**Expected**: an "unsupported format" style message, e.g. `unsupported audio: AC-3 is not supported`.

**Actual** (0.7.0): `soundcraft-cli: ac3_51.ac3: malformed audio: end of stream` (exit code 1); the same for `eac3_51.eac3`. The five AC-3/E-AC-3 soundtracks in our test set (extracted from MP4 and Matroska video) all give this message.

**Where**: apparently no format reader claims the file; symphonia's probe (0.5.5, `Probe::next`) then searches the data for a marker and runs into the end of the file with an I/O error, which `map_err` in `crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs` turns into `AudioError::Malformed`. Reporting a probe that finds no container as `Unsupported` would give the right message.

---
*Tested and written by Claude (Anthropic). Posted for Udo Funk (@KNUFFIXX), emotional support human, who reads every report after it goes out.*

title: MP3 import: frames whose last granule is empty are dropped, so the audio comes in shorter and shifted
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**SoundCraft 0.7.0 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11** (`soundcraft-cli`; main has the same symphonia 0.5.5)

Some valid MP3 frames fail to decode, and SoundCraft then leaves the frame out. The imported audio gets shorter than the file and everything after a dropped frame moves earlier. It happens with frames in which the earlier granules use up all of the frame's main data and the last granule (granule 1, right channel) has `part2_3_length` 0, which is legal and simply means that granule has no bits. The Windows Media Foundation MP3 encoder writes such frames (also used by Windows Media Player when it rips CDs) when one channel needs all the bits.

**Steps**

1. Fixture `mp3_mf320_left.mp3` (122 KB), written by [`make_fixtures_soundcraft.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/soundcraft/make_fixtures_soundcraft.py): 3.000 s, 44.1 kHz stereo, white noise on the left channel and digital silence on the right, encoded with ffmpeg 9.0.2's `mp3_mf` encoder at 320 kbps (Windows only; no Xing/Info frame, no ID3 tag). 27 of its 117 frames have the pattern, e.g. frame 0: `main_data_begin` 0, 1008 bytes of main data, `part2_3_length` 4092 + 852 + 3120 = 8064 bits (= 1008 bytes) and 0.
2. `soundcraft-cli info mp3_mf320_left.mp3`
3. `soundcraft-cli convert mp3_mf320_left.mp3 out.wav --bit-depth 32f` (`file.import_audio` gives the same length)

**Expected**: 134,784 frames, what `info` reports and what ffmpeg decodes.

**Actual** (0.7.0): `info` says 134,784 frames (3.056 s), but the converted file and the imported clip have 103,680 frames (2.351 s): 27 × 1152 frames are missing, and the audio after each gap starts early.

With real files: nine 320 kbps MP3s ripped from CD (no Xing/LAME tag, `main_data_begin` always 0, as the Media Foundation encoder writes them) came in 116–412 frames short (1–6 % of each track), most of the missing frames in the first and last seconds; already in the first 20 s 8–71 frames go missing, so the rest of the track is early by u…

title: AAC import: HE-AAC (SBR) files come in at half length, at double speed
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**SoundCraft 0.7.0 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11** (`soundcraft-cli`; main has the same symphonia 0.5.5)

HE-AAC (AAC-LC core plus SBR, the usual format of low-bitrate streams, voice messages and some TV recordings) imports with half the frames it should have. The AAC decoder only decodes the core, which runs at half the output rate, but the clip gets the output rate from the MP4 sample entry. The clip is therefore half as long as the file and plays an octave too high, at double speed.

**Steps**

1. An HE-AAC v1 file in MP4/M4A with implicit SBR signalling (the common case), for example `ffmpeg -i tone_mono_48k.wav -c:a libfdk_aac -profile:a aac_he -b:a 48k he.m4a` or, on macOS, `afconvert -f m4af -d aach -b 48000 tone_mono_48k.wav he.m4a` (`tone_mono_48k.wav` from [`make_fixtures_soundcraft.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/soundcraft/make_fixtures_soundcraft.py)). Synthetic fixtures: see **Fixtures** below.
2. `soundcraft-cli info he.m4a` and `soundcraft-cli convert he.m4a out.wav --bit-depth 32f`

**Expected**: the frame count ffprobe/ffmpeg give (output rate × duration), the audio at its normal pitch.

**Actual** (0.7.0), with two real-world HE-AAC files (a 270 s stereo soundtrack from a Matroska video and a 94 s voice message in M4A): `info` and `file.import_audio` report `"sample_rate": 48000` and exactly half the frames ffmpeg decodes (6,468,608 instead of 12,937,216; 2,244,608 instead of 4,489,216); the level envelope of the imported audio matches ffmpeg's decode only when stretched to twice its length.

**Where**: symphonia-codec-aac 0.5.5 has no SBR/PS decoder. With explicit signalling it refuses the file (`aac too complex`, `AacDecoder::try_new`); with implicit signalling it decodes the core and `run` in `crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs` keeps the sample rate from the container. Until SBR is supported, a check that the decoded frames per packet match the container's rate (2048 at the output rate vs. 1024 decoded) could at least…

title: Bounce report gives pre-clamp peak/true peak/LUFS while the 32-bit float file is clamped to ±1.0
author: tokuiten3
body:
## Summary

`file.bounce_mix` with `bit_depth: "32f"` writes samples clamped to [-1, 1], but the JSON result reports `peak_db` / `true_peak_db` (and `lufs`) measured before the clamp. The report says the file peaks at +3.5 dBFS while the written file never exceeds 0 dBFS.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a 1 s stereo 32-bit float WAV at 48 kHz containing a 440 Hz sine with amplitude 1.5 (`over.wav`).
2. Run `soundcraft-cli script repro.txt` with:

```
session.new {"sample_rate":48000}
file.import_audio {"paths":["over.wav"],"at":0}
file.bounce_mix {"path":"out.wav","bit_depth":"32f","dither":false,"normalize":false}
```

## Result

```
file.bounce_mix: {"bytes":384116,"lufs":2.838773012161255,"path":"out.wav","peak_db":3.521825075149536,"seconds":1.0,"true_peak_db":3.521825075149536}
```

- max |sample| of `over.wav`: 1.5
- max |sample| of `out.wav`: 1.0

The clamp comes from `clamp_float` in `crates/audio-io/src/pcm.rs` (used by the float WAV writer), so the clamp itself looks intentional; the issue is that the reported loudness/peak values describe a different signal from the file that was written.

## Expected

The reported `peak_db`, `true_peak_db` and `lufs` describe the samples actually written to the file (or the result states that the output was clipped and how many samples were affected).

## Environment

- commit f3a19480d8cc2d7a98cda492f5464d8c54558c9f (workspace version 0.7.0), `cargo build --release -p soundcraft-cli`
- macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon, rustc 1.98.0

title: AAC import: HE-AAC v2 (parametric stereo) files come in as mono
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**SoundCraft 0.8.0 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11** (also 0.7.0; `soundcraft-cli`, symphonia 0.5)

Split out of #712 as the triage bot asked there; #712 now covers only the length/speed part.

HE-AAC v2 carries a mono AAC core plus parametric stereo (PS) data, the usual format of low-bitrate voice messages and streams. SoundCraft imports such files with one channel. ffmpeg decodes them as stereo.

**Steps**

1. [`he_aac_v2_ps.m4a`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/soundcraft/he_aac_v2_ps.m4a): 440 Hz for 2 s, then 880 Hz for 2 s, the same signal on both channels, encoded with fdkaac 1.0.0 / libfdk-aac as HE-AAC v2 (implicit signalling). The sample entry declares 24000 Hz, so the speed problem of #712 does not show up here.
2. `soundcraft-cli info he_aac_v2_ps.m4a`, then `file.import_audio` in a session.

**Expected**: 2 channels (ffprobe: `HE-AACv2`, 2 channels; ffmpeg decodes stereo).

**Actual** (0.7.0 and 0.8.0, 2026-10-18, identical):

```
"channels": 1, "format": "Aac", "frames": 100352, "sample_rate": 24000
```

The HE-AAC v1 file of the same signal ([`he_aac_v1_stereo.m4a`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/soundcraft/he_aac_v1_stereo.m4a), stereo core) imports with 2 channels, so only the PS case loses the second channel.

**Where**: symphonia-codec-aac 0.5.x decodes only the AAC-LC core and has no PS decoder, so the channel count comes from the mono core. Until PS is supported, the importer could at least warn that the file is HE-AAC v2 and is imported as mono.

title: Web build: a host bridge for embedding pages (?host=parent), like PdfCraft's
author: philkunz
body:
We run the SoundCraft web build as a window in a web desktop that frames the web build, the same way as PdfCraft, GridCraft and CADCraft. Their `?host=parent` bridge lets the embedding page open files and receive saves. Without one, SoundCraft can't tell the page about unsaved changes, so the page can't ask before a window with edits closes, and saves become browser downloads.

Proposal, the same family protocol as storytold/deckcraft#983 and storytold/wordcraft#2919, posted to the parent only with `?host=parent`:
- `soundcrafteady` / `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-philkunz-foss-global/410470bf-81b1-4e09-9a60-86819268a2c6/scratchpad/issues/soundcraftiled`: start-up handshake
- `soundcraft:open {name, bytes}`: the parent hands over a file to open
- `soundcraftve, Save As and exports go to the parent instead of a download
- `soundcraft:dirty {dirty}`: on every change of the unsaved state

title: [Bug] Record-arm and input-monitoring states persist across sessions
author: SlyLaM
body:
## Description

SoundCraft currently stores each track’s `record_arm` and `input_monitor` states in the session document.

When a session is saved while tracks are record-enabled or input-monitored, these states are serialized. Reopening the session restores them, and the UI may then open the audio input device automatically.

This can activate a live input path immediately after opening a session, without an explicit action from the user. Depending on the routing and monitoring configuration, this may cause feedback, loud transients, or other unexpected output.

Record enable and input monitoring should be temporary runtime states rather than persistent session data.

## Expected behavior

- Record enable and input monitoring remain functional while the session is open.
- Saving or autosaving a session does not store either state.
- Opening or recovering a session initializes both states to `false`.
- Existing session files containing `record_arm: true` or `input_monitor: true` ignore those saved values.
- Opening a session does not activate or open an input path because of previously saved arm or monitoring states.
- Changing either state does not mark the session as modified.
- Changing either state does not add an entry to the document Undo/Redo history.
- Routing and other persistent track settings remain unchanged.

## Implementation notes

`Mixer::record_arm` and `Mixer::input_monitor` currently belong to the serialized `Session` model.

Simply excluding them from Serde serialization may prevent them from being written or restored, but it will not by itself make them fully transient.

The implementation must also ensure that changes to these fields are excluded from:

- session dirty-state comparison;
- document Undo/Redo history;
- autosaved session data.

This may be implemented by separating the states from persistent mixer data, or by explicitly treating them as transient throughout serialization, dirty-state comparison, and command handling.

author: iannitram
body:
On Windows, `io::save_tests::saved_audio_is_trusted_only_in_the_folder_it_was_saved_in` (crates/engine/src/io.rs) fails on plain `main` (25d52c6). The code under test looks right: only the test's expected value is wrong on Windows.

```
cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib -- saved_audio_is_trusted_only
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: ["%TEMP%\\soundcraft-own-folder-<pid>\\A\\Audio Files\\Audio 1_02.wav"]
 right: ["%TEMP%\\soundcraft-own-folder-<pid>\\A\\Audio Files/Audio 1_02.wav"]
```

The expected path is built as `dir.join("A").join("Audio Files/Audio 1_02.wav")`, which keeps the `/` on Windows, while `open_session` reports the native path with `\`. Joining the parts separately (`.join("Audio Files").join("Audio 1_02.wav")`) should make the test pass on every OS. Found while running the workspace tests on Windows 11 (x64, rustc 1.95); on Linux and macOS the two spellings are the same, which is why CI doesn't see it.

title: Web build: report the open document in the viewport title
author: robertcsakany
body:
The web build sends no `ViewportCommand::Title` naming the open document (eframe would log it as `Unhandled egui viewport command: Title(…)` on the web). WordCraft, GridCraft, PhotoCraft and VectorCraft do (`<document>[ •] — <App>`).

title: mix.send to an unknown bus name silently creates a new bus instead of reporting an error
author: chazmaniandinkle
body:
## Summary

`mix.send` with a `bus` name that does not exist creates a new stereo bus with that name and returns success (`{"bus":N,"slot":0}`). Nothing in the result says a bus was created. A typo in a bus name therefore sends the signal to a new bus that no track listens to, and the mix is silently wrong. In Pro Tools a send can only target an existing bus, or a new one created explicitly through the send selector's New Track / New Bus dialog.

## Environment

SoundCraft CLI 0.8.0, Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200).

## Steps to reproduce

```
soundcraft-cli run --cmd 'session.new={"name":"S2"}' \
  --cmd 'track.new={"kind":"audio","name":"Gtr"}' \
  --cmd 'mix.new_bus={"name":"Verb"}' \
  --cmd 'mix.send={"track":"Gtr","bus":"Nowhere"}' \
  --cmd 'mix.send={"track":"Gtr","slot":1,"bus":"verb"}' \
  --inspect
```

## Actual

```
mix.new_bus: {"bus":2}
mix.send: {"bus":3,"slot":0}
mix.send: {"bus":2,"slot":1}
```
`busses`: `[{"id":2,"name":"Verb"},{"id":3,"name":"Nowhere"}]`. Bus 3 was created implicitly by the send and nothing takes input from it. (`"verb"` matches `Verb` case-insensitively.) No error, no warning, no `created` flag.

## Expected

Either an error such as `no bus named "Nowhere"`, consistent with `mix.insert` / `mix.insert_param`, which reject unknown parameter names. Or, if auto-creation is meant as a scripting convenience, make it opt-in (e.g. `create_bus: true`) and return `"created": true`.

## Workaround

Create busses explicitly with `mix.new_bus` first, and check `busses` in `session.inspect` after adding sends.

title: Control channel: requests time out when no frame is rendered, but stay queued and run later
author: teil3
body:
**Version:** 0.8.0 (also seen on 0.6.1), Linux x86_64, Ubuntu 26.04, GNOME on Wayland. The code path is unchanged on `main`.

## What happens

When the app is driven over the control channel (`soundcraft --control 7878`, either via `soundcraft-cli mcp --connect 7878` or raw TCP), requests often take up to 90 s and then return `{"ok": false, "error": "timeout"}`. The app is idle at the time (≈2 % CPU).

The timed-out request is **not dropped**. It stays queued and runs later. A client cannot tell "timeout" apart from "not executed".

## Measurements on 0.8.0

Fresh start, empty session, raw TCP, no MCP in between:

| Request | Round trip |
|---|---|
| `session.inspect` (first request after start) | 47.5 s |
| `ui.inspect` ×3 back to back | 51.0 s, 0.13 s, 0.13 s |
| `ui.inspect` after a 1 s / 3 s / 10 s pause | 90 s → `timeout`, each time |

Once a frame runs, follow-up requests are fast. When the app goes idle again, the next request stalls.

## Evidence that timed-out requests still execute

- A `batch` of 106 `midi.note_add` calls: 41 ok, then call 42 got `timeout` and the batch stopped. The clip afterwards held **42** notes.
- `clip.clear` and `event.retrospective_record` both returned `timeout`, and their effects showed up later.
- A `batch` with `keep_going: true` of 44 calls: 6 got `timeout`, but the final session contained everything exactly once (requests on one connection are serialized, so the order held).

## Cause (from reading the source)

`apps/soundcraft/src/control_server.rs`, `serve()`: the request is sent to the UI channel, then `ctx.request_repaint()` is called, then the server waits on `rrx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(90))`. The request is only handled in `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` `drain()`, i.e. inside an egui frame. Calling `request_repaint()` from the server thread apparently does not wake the event loop here, possibly because the window is not focused or visible on Wayland. The request then waits until some other event produces a f…

title: Docs: MIDI tick resolution (960 PPQ) is not stated for tick-based midi.* commands
author: teil3
body:
**Version:** 0.8.0, also on `main`.

`midi.note_add` documents `{clip, pitch, start_ticks, length_ticks?: 480, …}`. The same tick fields appear in `midi.note_edit`, `midi.notes_move`, `event.midi_note` and `event.retrospective_record`, but nowhere (`engine.commands` params text, MCP server instructions, `docs/control-protocol.md`, `docs/mcp.md`) does it say how many ticks a quarter note has.

The default `length_ticks: 480` reads like a quarter note at 480 PPQ, which is a common DAW resolution. `crates/midi/src/lib.rs` defines `PPQ = 960`, though, so 480 is an eighth note. A scripted 8-bar song written at 480 PPQ ends up at half speed: every note lands at half its intended position and length, and the whole arrangement collapses into the first half of each clip. Nothing reports an error.

## Suggestion

- State "960 ticks per quarter note (one 4/4 bar = 3840)" in the params text of the tick-based MIDI commands and in the MCP instructions.
- Optionally, accept the position strings the rest of the API already supports (`"bars_beats:5|1|000"`, `{"seconds": …}`) for note start, and note values (`"1/8"`) for length, so callers don't have to know the PPQ at all.

title: FreeBSD aarch64 CI: bounce.rs test exceeds Harness max_steps (x86_64 passes)
author: iannitram
body:
The scheduled FreeBSD workflow fails on the aarch64 job in `crates/ui-egui/tests/bounce.rs`, while the x86_64 FreeBSD job of the same run passes.

- Run: https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/actions/runs/39366640137 (2026-10-20, `main`)
- Job: `FreeBSD 15 aarch64 (build + test)` (the `FreeBSD 15 x86_64` job in the same run passes)
- Test: `a_bounce_renders_across_frames_with_progress_until_its_file_is_written`
- Location: `crates/ui-egui/tests/bounce.rs:55:7`

Panic from the job log:

```
thread 'a_bounce_renders_across_frames_with_progress_until_its_file_is_written' (110655) panicked at crates/ui-egui/tests/bounce.rs:55:7:
Harness::run exceeded max_steps (1000). If your expect your ui to keep repainting (e.g. when showing a spinner) call Harness::step or Harness::run_steps instead.
```

The aarch64 job runs under QEMU emulation and takes over 4 hours. A fork of the repo shows the same failure. I read this from the CI logs and did not reproduce it locally.

What the test does at that line: the harness is built with `with_max_steps(1_000)`. The test starts a Bounce Mix from the dialog, steps four frames while checking that progress increases and stays below 1.0, then line 55 calls `h.run()` to run frames until the bounce finishes and the app stops requesting repaints. The panic means that on aarch64 the UI was still requesting repaints after 1000 steps.

Guess, not verified: the bounce render is much slower under emulation, so it may need more than 1000 harness frames to finish (for example if each frame renders a bounded slice of audio), or the render is finishing but something keeps requesting repaints. The logs do not tell these apart.

AI-assisted: yes

title: [Bug Report] [SoundCraft] save_session with a bare file name fails with "path is empty" when roots are set
author: forhadkhan
body:
## Environment
- SoundCraft 0.11.0 (`soundcraft-cli --version`), Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, .deb from ArtCraft Launcher 0.6.1
- Driven by an MCP client over stdio: `soundcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root <dir> --automation-write-root <dir>`, working directory `<dir>`

## Steps (JSON tool calls)
1. `new_session` `{"name":"t","sample_rate":48000}`
2. `execute` `{"command":"track.new","params":{"kind":"audio","name":"Tone","format":"mono"}}`
3. `save_session` `{"path":"t.scraft"}`

## Expected
The session is saved as `t.scraft` in the working directory (inside the write root).

## Actual
Step 3 fails: `automation path rejected: path is empty`.

`{"path":"./t.scraft"}` works. `bounce_mix` with a bare name (`{"path":"bare.wav", ...}`) also works. Started without the `--automation-*-root` flags, a bare `save_session` path works too, so the root check seems to lose a path that has no directory part.

title: [Bug Report] [SoundCraft] Master mix.trim has no effect, and master mix.volume is ignored when volume automation exists
author: forhadkhan
body:
## Environment
- SoundCraft 0.11.0 (`soundcraft-cli --version`), Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, .deb from ArtCraft Launcher 0.6.1
- Driven by an MCP client over stdio: `soundcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root <dir> --automation-write-root <dir>`, working directory `<dir>`

## Steps (JSON tool calls)
1. `new_session` `{"name":"t","sample_rate":48000}`
2. `execute` `track.new` `{"kind":"audio","name":"Tone","format":"mono"}`, then `execute` `track.new` `{"kind":"master"}` (the master is named `Master 1`)
3. `execute` `edit.select` `{"tracks":["Tone"],"start":{"seconds":0},"end":{"seconds":2}}`, then `audiosuite.process` `{"process":"signal_generator","params":{"waveform":0,"freq":440,"level":-12}}`
4. `bounce_mix` `{"path":"./a.wav","format":"wav","bit_depth":24}` returns `lufs` -15.68, `peak_db` -15.0.
5. `execute` `mix.trim` `{"tracks":["Master 1"],"db":-12}` returns `{"db": -12.0}`. Bounce again: still -15.68 LUFS, -15.0 peak.
6. Reset trim to 0. `execute` `mix.volume` `{"tracks":["Master 1"],"db":-12}`. Bounce: -27.68 LUFS (works).
7. Reset volume to 0. Add `automation.set_point` `{"track":"Master 1","param":"volume","at":{"seconds":0},"value":0}` and the same at 2 seconds. Then `mix.volume` `{"tracks":["Master 1"],"db":-12}`. Bounce: -15.68 LUFS again.

## Expected
Master `mix.trim` changes the level, or the command returns an error that says the master has no trim. A `mix.volume` that cannot take effect (volume automation is in read mode) returns a warning or error.

## Actual
Both return success and change nothing. The caller only finds out by bouncing and measuring.

title: [Bug Report] [SoundCraft] automation.clear without a range leaves the last breakpoint, so a cleared master stays at -80 dB
author: forhadkhan
body:
## Environment
- SoundCraft 0.11.0 (`soundcraft-cli --version`), Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, .deb from ArtCraft Launcher 0.6.1
- Driven by an MCP client over stdio: `soundcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root <dir> --automation-write-root <dir>`, working directory `<dir>`

## Steps (JSON tool calls)
1. `new_session` `{"name":"t","sample_rate":48000}`, then `track.new` `{"kind":"audio","name":"Tone","format":"mono"}` and `track.new` `{"kind":"master"}`
2. `edit.select` `{"tracks":["Tone"],"start":{"seconds":0},"end":{"seconds":2}}`, then `audiosuite.process` `{"process":"signal_generator","params":{"waveform":0,"freq":440,"level":-12}}`
3. `automation.set_point` on `{"track":"Master 1","param":"volume"}` with `{"at":{"seconds":0},"value":-80}`, `0.5` s value 0, `1.5` s value 0, `2` s value -80.
4. `bounce_mix` `{"path":"./f.wav","format":"wav","bit_depth":24}`: -17.2 LUFS (fade in and out as expected).
5. `execute` `automation.clear` `{"track":"Master 1"}` returns `{"removed": 3}` (four points were set).
6. `bounce_mix` again: `lufs` -144.0, `peak_db` -95.0.
7. `inspect_session`: the master still has `"automation": [{"param": "volume", "points": 1}]`.

## Expected
`automation.clear` with no range removes all points. The volume lane is empty and the master plays at its fader value.

## Actual
The last breakpoint (-80 dB) stays, so the whole master is held at -80 dB and the bounce is silent. Passing `start` and `end` for the full range is the workaround.

title: [Feature Request] [SoundCraft] Choose the output sample rate in bounce_mix
author: forhadkhan
body:
## Environment
- SoundCraft 0.11.0 (`soundcraft-cli --version`), Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, .deb from ArtCraft Launcher 0.6.1
- Driven by an MCP client over stdio: `soundcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root <dir> --automation-write-root <dir>`, working directory `<dir>`

## Request
`bounce_mix` has no way to choose the output sample rate. Its schema is `path, format, bit_depth, normalize, start, end`, and the file is written at the session rate.

A session at 48 kHz that must be delivered at 44.1 kHz (or the reverse) needs a second tool. A `sample_rate` argument on `bounce_mix`, with a high-quality resampler, would keep the whole job in SoundCraft.

Related: #717 (bounce report) and #791 (32-bit float clipping) touch the same tool.

title: [Feature Request] [SoundCraft] LUFS and true-peak targets for bounce_mix normalize
author: forhadkhan
body:
## Environment
- SoundCraft 0.11.0 (`soundcraft-cli --version`), Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, .deb from ArtCraft Launcher 0.6.1
- Driven by an MCP client over stdio: `soundcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root <dir> --automation-write-root <dir>`, working directory `<dir>`

## Request
`bounce_mix` has `normalize: true`, which peak-normalizes to -0.1 dBFS. It cannot target a loudness. Delivery specs usually give an integrated LUFS target and a true-peak ceiling (for example -16 LUFS and -1 dBTP).

Please add optional `target_lufs` and `true_peak_ceiling_db` arguments (or a loudness-normalize mode) to `bounce_mix`. The report already returns `lufs` and `true_peak_db`, so the measurement exists. Today a caller must bounce, read the numbers, adjust faders and bounce again.

Related: #717 (bounce report gives pre-clamp values).

title: [Feature Request] [SoundCraft] Accept more than one --automation-read-root / --automation-write-root
author: forhadkhan
body:
## Environment
- SoundCraft 0.11.0 (`soundcraft-cli --version`), Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, .deb from ArtCraft Launcher 0.6.1
- Driven by an MCP client over stdio

## Steps
```
soundcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /tmp --automation-read-root /var
soundcraft-cli mcp --automation-write-root /tmp --automation-write-root /var
```

## Actual
Both exit at once with:
```
soundcraft-cli: --automation-read-root given twice
```
(and the same for `--automation-write-root`).

## Expected / request
Allow each option more than once (or a list of folders), so one MCP session can read from a project folder and a shared assets folder, or write to an output folder and a scratch folder, without widening the root to their common parent. The confinement stays as strict as today: only the listed folders are allowed.

Other Craft apps (PhotoCraft, EffectCraft, FigCraft) already accept the option twice.

title: [Audit] Unauthenticated control channel, reachable cross-protocol, with arbitrary file write
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

Supersedes #459 (closed without a fix; still present).

**Code:** [`apps/soundcraft/src/control_server.rs:28, 97-138`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/apps/soundcraft/src/control_server.rs#L28), [`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:300`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs#L300)

**Evidence:**
- `control_server.rs:28` binds `127.0.0.1` with no token, handshake or peer check.
- The serve loop answers a line that is not JSON and **keeps reading** (`control_server.rs:132-136`):
  ```rust
  Err(e) => json!({"ok": false, "error": format!("bad JSON: {e}")}),
  };
  if writeln!(out, "{reply}").is_err() { break; }
  ```
- `ui.screenshot` writes the PNG to any path it is given (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:300`):
  ```rust
  Some(p) => match std::fs::write(p, &bytes) {
  ```
- The desktop app never installs automation roots, so `check_write` and `check_read` let everything through. `parse_mcp_args` refuses roots together with `--connect`.
- The accepted stream never gets `set_read_timeout`; the only calls are in tests (`:192`, `:209`).

- **Web page.** The protocol is line-based and answers non-JSON lines with an error instead of closing, so the body of a cross-origin HTTP request to the port is processed as commands after the request line and headers are rejected. Chromium's Local Network Access prompt, where enforced, interrupts this; other browsers and form posts **need verification**.

title: [Audit] Matroska/EBML element size triggers a 128 TiB allocation and aborts the process
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs:56-67`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs#L56-L67)

- **Severity:** High. **Confidence:** **Confirmed, reproduced at 9b8283b.** A fix was proposed in #746 (closed unmerged). The only `symph.rs` change upstream, 8840fbc, affects the `fLaC` arm.

**Evidence:**
- `crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs:56-67` runs pre-checks only for these formats:
  ```rust
  Some(b"caff") => crate::caf::check(bytes, at)?,
  Some(b"ftyp") => crate::mp4::check(bytes, at.saturating_sub(4))?,
  Some(b"fLaC") => { crate::flac::check_metadata(bytes, at)?; … }
  Some(b"RIFF") => crate::wav::check_info(bytes, at)?,
  _ => {}
  ```
- `Cargo.toml:39` still enables symphonia's `"mkv"` feature, and `Cargo.lock` pins symphonia 0.5.5.
- `symphonia-format-mkv-0.5.5/src/ebml.rs:480,485` calls `read_boxed_slice_exact(header.data_len as usize)`, which becomes `vec![0u8; len]` (`symphonia-core-0.5.5/src/io/mod.rs:344`). Children are checked against their parent, never against the file length.

**Reproduction.** Built `--release` against the repo's `Cargo.lock`, a 30-byte EBML header whose EBML and DocType element sizes are far larger than the file, passed to `soundcraft_audio_io::probe(&bytes, Some("wav"))`, prints `memory allocation of 140737488355328 bytes failed` and exits. (The exact bytes are left out of this public issue; happy to share privately.)
This is an allocation-failure abort, so no `catch_unwind` can catch it.

**Impact:**
- The desktop app crashes on import, drag and drop, sampler load or clip-group import.
- A session that references such a file (under any name) aborts at **every** open: a crash loop for a shared project.
- Combined with #877, it can be triggered remotely.
- On web, the tab dies.

title: [Audit] H.264 picture size is unbounded, and frame_num-gap concealment allocates up to 65,535 pictures
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

Supersedes #427, #429 (closed without a fix; still present).

**Code:** [`crates/video/src/h264/params.rs:398`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/video/src/h264/params.rs#L398)

- **Severity:** High. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code; not reproduced.

**Evidence:**
- **Size bound.** `crates/video/src/h264/params.rs:398` is the only bound on coded size. It allows 16384×16384, 4× the crate's own `MAX_PIXELS = 8192*8192` (`movie.rs:13`):
  ```rust
  ensure!(pic_width_in_mbs <= 1024 && pic_height_in_map_units <= 1024, "picture too large");
  ```
- **No cross-check.** `MAX_PIXELS` is checked only against the container size (`movie.rs:257`), ProRes (`:405`) and JPEG (`:421`). H.264 never compares the SPS with either.
- **Gap branch.** `decoder.rs:446-475` (non-IDR) enters gap concealment whenever `frame_num` jumps. It never reads `sps.gaps_in_frame_num_allowed`, which is parsed at `params.rs:395` and only stored.
- **Allocation loop.** `dpb.rs:136-154` loops up to `max_frame_num` (65,536) times. Each step allocates full planes plus `Frame::from_planes`, which also allocates an `MbState` per macroblock (`picture.rs:247-255`):
  ```rust
  while unused != frame_num && guard < max_frame_num {
  ```

**Scenario:**
1. An `avc1` track declares 320×240 in its sample entry, so it opens.
2. Its avcC SPS declares 1024×1024 MBs, `max_num_ref_frames = 16` and `log2_max_frame_num = 16`.
3. The first sample is a P slice with `frame_num = 65535`.
4. Both `decode_h264` (`movie.rs:447`) and the thumbnail path `decode_h264_single` (`:437`) reach the loop: about 65,534 iterations of at least 400 MB each, with about 16 pictures kept live, at least 6.4 GB.

**Impact:**
- Native: abort on allocation failure. Otherwise a near-permanent hang of the single video-decode worker.
- Web: the tab freezes or dies (decode runs on the UI thread).

title: [Audit] Signing secrets are exposed to every dependency's build code
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`packaging/macos/{import-cert,package}.sh`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/packaging/macos/), [`packaging/windows/package.ps1:65`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/packaging/windows/package.ps1#L65)

- **Severity:** High. **Confidence:** Confirmed (workflow config, read at `craft-common-actions@a4acae8e`). Exploitation requires a malicious crate or `build.rs` in the 538-crate graph.

**Evidence:**
- **macOS.** `craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/release.yml:222-235` imports the Developer ID certificate into a keychain that `packaging/macos/import-cert.sh:28-33` leaves unlocked for 6 hours, with `/usr/bin/security` on the key's ACL:
  ```sh
  security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$KEYCHAIN"
  security import "$CERT" -P "${APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD:-}" -T /usr/bin/codesign -T /usr/bin/security ...
  ```
  The next step, "Build, sign, notarize", sets `APPLE_ID`/`APPLE_PASSWORD`/`APPLE_TEAM_ID` and runs `packaging/macos/package.sh`, which compiles in that environment (`package.sh:61`):
  ```sh
  (cd "$ROOT" && cargo build --release --locked -p soundcraft -p soundcraft-cli "${args[@]}")
  ```
- **Windows.** The "Build, sign, package" step (`release.yml:362-375`) sets `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE(_PASSWORD)` and `AZURE_TENANT_ID/CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET` and runs `package.ps1`, which runs `cargo build` at `:65` before signing.

**Scenario:** a hijacked or typosquatted transitive crate, possibly arriving through the grouped daily Dependabot PR (#900), runs code in its `build.rs` or proc-macro. That code can:
- read the Azure client secret from the environment and sign arbitrary binaries as the publisher until the secret is rotated;
- exfiltrate the PFX and its password;
- use `codesign` against the unlocked keychain, and plausibly export the key;
- take the notarization credentials.

title: [Audit] The release pipeline runs from a mutable, unprotected shared `@main`
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`.github/workflows/release.yml:13-14, 23, 28-42`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/.github/workflows/release.yml#L13-L14)

- **Severity:** High. **Confidence:** Confirmed (config). Per the GitHub API at the time of the audit, the shared repo's `main` has `protected: false` and no rulesets.

**Evidence:**
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:23`:
  ```yaml
  uses: storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/release.yml@main
  ```
  It is called with `permissions: contents: write` (`:13-14`) and every signing secret passed explicitly (`:28-42`).
- The same `@main` pattern is used in `freebsd.yml:32`, `nix.yml:23`, `packaging-lint.yml:23`, `sonarcloud.yml:19` and `windows-arm64.yml:30`.
- The `release` environment is declared inside the called workflow, so its branch policy cannot pin what code runs.

**Scenario:** anyone with push access to `craft-common-actions`, or a leaked token for it, changes `main`. The next push to `release` in any craft repo runs that code with signing secrets and write access. Dependabot cannot see branch refs, so nothing flags the change.

**Fix:**
- Pin by commit SHA (`…/release.yml@a4acae8e3a54b0c198c9f22fe4f4197ffd9f58b8`) and let Dependabot bump it.
- Protect `main` in the shared repo, and use relative or SHA refs inside it.
- Add required reviewers to the `release` environment.

title: [Audit] Decompression amplification to 4 GiB; allocation failure aborts
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/audio-io/src/pcm.rs:8`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/audio-io/src/pcm.rs#L8)

- **Severity:** Medium (High on web). **Confidence:** Confirmed by code; the ratio is estimated.
- **Evidence:**
  - `crates/audio-io/src/pcm.rs:8` sets `MAX_DECODE_SAMPLES: u64 = (4u64 << 30) / 4;`.
  - `symph.rs:163-168` caps up front only when `n_frames` is known. Otherwise `symph.rs:224-244` grows the output with infallible `dst.push(...)` and checks afterwards.
  - The engine's `MAX_IMPORT_SAMPLES` is the same 1 G (`engine/src/io.rs:12`).
  - `try_reserve` is used only in the encoders.
  - The new `flac::empty_stream_info` (8840fbc) helps only when no frames follow the metadata.
- **Scenario:** a FLAC with total samples = 0, 8 channels, and CONSTANT subframes in 65,535-sample blocks. About 74 KB decodes to about 4 GiB of f32, plus peaks and a resample copy. A session can reference several such files.
- **Impact:** multi-GB memory use and a UI freeze on desktop, an abort on low-RAM machines, and the wasm tab dies.
- **Fix sketch:**
  ```diff
  -pub(crate) const MAX_DECODE_SAMPLES: u64 = (4u64 << 30) / 4;
  +pub(crate) const MAX_DECODE_SAMPLES: u64 = if cfg!(target_pointer_width = "32") { 1 << 26 } else { 1 << 30 };
  // symph.rs: dst.try_reserve(n).map_err(|_| AudioError::TooLarge)? before each push batch
  // engine: decode_with_limit(bytes, hint, remaining_session_budget)
  ```

title: [Audit] The automation-roots check stats attacker paths before refusing them (NTLM leak)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/file_access.rs:197-242`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/file_access.rs#L197-L242)

- **Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code. The SMB behaviour is standard Windows and was not exercised.
- **Evidence:** in `crates/engine/src/file_access.rs:197-242`, the only lexical gate is the DOS-device check (`:202`). It is followed by `std::path::absolute` (`:205`), `std::fs::canonicalize(at)` (`:210`) and `symlink_metadata` (`:215`). The roots are compared only afterwards, in `check` (`:100`).
- **Scenario:** `soundcraft-cli mcp` is started with an automation read root, and a prompt-injected agent passes a UNC path to `file.import_audio` (`cmd/file.rs:58` → `io::read_file` → `check_read` → `resolve`). Windows opens an SMB connection to that host and sends the NTLMv2 response before the path is refused.
- **Contrast:** session-stored paths go through `craft_docpath::resolve`, which refuses UNC paths lexically.
- **Fix sketch:**
  ```diff
   fn resolve(path: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
  +    if cfg!(windows) && matches!(path.components().next(), Some(Component::Prefix(p))
  +        if matches!(p.kind(), Prefix::UNC(..) | Prefix::VerbatimUNC(..) | Prefix::DeviceNS(_) | Prefix::Verbatim(_))) {
  +        return Err(format!("automation path rejected: network/device paths are not allowed: {}", path.display()));
  +    }
  ```

title: [Audit] Unclamped clip-FX gain and send-level automation (up to +200 dB)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/mix/src/lib.rs:1197-1198, 1754-1762`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/mix/src/lib.rs#L1197-L1198)

- **Severity:** Medium (hearing and equipment risk; the output clamp limits it to 0 dBFS). **Confidence:** Confirmed. 52dc4f9 added only the state reset. A fix was proposed in #748 (closed unmerged).
- **Evidence:**
  - Clip FX store the gain raw (`crates/mix/src/lib.rs:1197-1198`):
    ```rust
    } else if k == "gain" {
        self.gain_db = v;
    ```
  - `send_level` (`:1754-1762`) returns `l.value_at(pos, base)` raw.
  - `clip_fx_params` (`:1108-1122`) casts `*v as f32`, so a huge finite f64 becomes ±inf.
  - `db_to_gain` (`dsp/src/lib.rs:360-361`) caps at `db.min(200.0)`.
  - Session sanitize keeps lane values if they are finite (`model/src/session.rs:579-583`). `AutoParam::range()` exists (`model/src/automation.rs:108-115`) but is not applied.
  - `clip.effects_set` accepts any finite f64 (`cmd/clip_more.rs:177-188`).
  - The fixed `snd.level_db` *is* clamped (`model/src/mixer.rs:563`).
- **Scenario:** a shared session with `clip_fx.<id>.gain = 500` or a `SendLevel` point of 300, or an MCP `clip.effects_set {"params":{"gain":1e6}}`. A full-scale clipped blast plays the moment playback reaches it.
- **Fix sketch:**
  ```diff
   l.points.retain(|p| p.value.is_finite());
  +let (lo, hi, _) = l.param.range();
  +l.points.iter_mut().for_each(|p| p.value = p.value.clamp(lo, hi));
  -self.gain_db = v;
  +self.gain_db = v.clamp(-144.0, 24.0);
  ```
  Also apply `.min(12.0)` in `send_level` and clamp in `clip.effects_set`.

title: [Audit] VST3 edit-controller method called from the audio thread
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

Supersedes #434 (closed without a fix; still present).

**Code:** [`crates/vst3-host/src/plugin.rs:140`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/vst3-host/src/plugin.rs#L140)

- **Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** Confirmed for the code path; Plausible for the plugin-side crash. Widened by 783ce8f.
- **Evidence:**
  - `crates/vst3-host/src/plugin.rs:39-42` documents that `set_param` "never calls the controller". Yet `normalized_from_plain` (`:131-144`), which `set_param` (`:222-239`) calls, does this at `:140`:
    ```rust
    Mapping::Plain => self.inst.to_normalized(id, f64::from(v)).unwrap_or(linear),
    ```
  - That reaches `Instance::to_normalized` → `plainParamToNormalized` (`ffi.rs:1244-1252`) without the `EditorLink` lock. The caller is `MixEngine::render` → `apply_values` (`mix/src/lib.rs:1681-1691`).
- **New:** 783ce8f's `Vst3Editor::value_text` (`plugin.rs:504-518` → `EditorLink::value_text`, `ffi.rs:1791-1803`) calls `getParamStringByValue` on the UI thread for every visible parameter row, every frame. During automated playback, concurrent controller calls are therefore far more frequent.
- **Impact:** a data race inside plugin code (UB in the plugin, a possible crash), plus locking or allocation on the audio thread.
- **Fix:** sample `to_plain` into a table on the UI thread in `Vst3Plugin::new`, and invert it with a binary search in `set_param`. Never cross the FFI boundary from the audio thread for controller methods.

title: [Audit] The audio callback blocks on rayon's global pool
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

Supersedes #438 (closed without a fix; still present).

**Code:** [`crates/mix/src/lib.rs:1283-1295`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/mix/src/lib.rs#L1283-L1295)

- **Severity:** Medium (dropouts). **Confidence:** Confirmed by code and rayon's documented behaviour.
- **Evidence:** `crates/mix/src/lib.rs:1283-1295` (called from `:658`):
  ```rust
  if work.len() >= 4 {
      let audio = on_audio_thread();
      work.par_iter_mut().for_each(|w| as_audio_thread(audio, || f(w)));
  ```
  The cpal thread is not a rayon worker, so it parks on a `LockLatch` (Mutex and Condvar). Bounces, freeze and previews share the global pool. The only dedicated pool belongs to the H.264 decoder (`video/src/h264/decoder.rs:156`).
- **Fix:** `if work.len() >= 4 && !on_audio_thread()`, or a dedicated pool built in `Player::open` that is never shared with offline work.

title: [Audit] Control-channel slowloris and memory amplification
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`apps/soundcraft/src/control_server.rs:20-24, 55-71`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/apps/soundcraft/src/control_server.rs#L20-L24)

- **Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** Confirmed for the missing timeout; Plausible for the exact figures.
- **Evidence:** `control_server.rs:20-24` (`MAX_LINE` about 86 MiB, `MAX_CONNECTIONS = 16`) and `:55-71`; there is no `set_read_timeout` in `serve`. `read_until` grows by doubling and `buf.clear()` keeps the capacity, so about 1.35 GiB is touched and up to about 2 GiB committed.
- **Scenario:** 16 idle connections lock out every legitimate client indefinitely.
- **Fix:** a read timeout, a cap on total buffered bytes across connections, and a smaller line cap with a separate path for large plugin states. All of this comes on top of #877's authentication.

title: [Audit] Long recorded takes are dropped from the session
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/io.rs:1452-1454`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L1452-L1454)

- **Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** Confirmed. The code moved with 6b4a7da's punch handling.
- **Evidence:** `crates/engine/src/io.rs:1452-1454`:
  ```rust
  read_file(&path).and_then(|b| soundcraft_audio_io::decode(&b, None)...);
  let Ok((_, buf)) = read.inspect_err(|err| e.message(err.to_string())) else { continue };
  ```
  The recorder writes f32 WAV/RF64 with no length cap (`playback/src/record.rs:385-401`). Decoding caps at 1 G samples: about 46.6 min of stereo at 192 kHz, or 23 min of 8 channels at 96 kHz. The take stays on disk; no clip is placed; the only notice is a status message.
- **Fix:** roll over to a new take file before `MAX_IMPORT_SAMPLES / channels` frames, or place an offline clip and raise a blocking error.

title: [Audit] A latency change reallocates and zeroes delay lines in the callback
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/mix/src/lib.rs:260-267`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/mix/src/lib.rs#L260-L267)

- **Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** Confirmed. See also #919.
- **Evidence:** `crates/mix/src/lib.rs:260-267`, called every block at `:707, 710, 718, 741, 743`:
  ```rust
  if len != self.len || self.bufs.len() != ch {
      self.len = len; self.idx = 0;
      self.bufs = vec![vec![0.0; len]; ch];
  ```
  The compressor's `lookahead` is automatable and is reported as latency (`dsp/src/plugins/dynamics.rs:44, 113, 192-193`). only strips whose delay length changes reallocate, which is all of them when the maximum latency moves. One allocation can reach 2^20 × channels f32.
- **Fix:** grow only and keep the contents, or pre-size each line to the maximum latency in `sync` and change only the read offset.

title: [Audit] SMF tempo and track floods
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

Related: #454 (33d59b2).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/io.rs:294-312`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L294-L312)

- **Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** Plausible (performance not measured). 705c2b9 only range-checks tempos at session load, and 33d59b2 widens the track flood.
- **Evidence:**
  - Meters are capped (`MAX_MIDI_METERS = 10_000`, `crates/engine/src/io.rs:291, 299-301`), but tempos are not (`:302-304`):
    ```rust
    for (tick, bpm) in &smf.tempos { let _ = s.tempo.set_tempo(*tick, *bpm); }
    ```
  - `time/src/tempo.rs:206-237` scans linearly per conversion; conversions run per note and per click on the audio thread. `midi/src/smf.rs:8,10` allows `MAX_EVENTS = 5_000_000` and `MAX_TRACKS = 4096`.
- **New:** 33d59b2 keeps controller-only tracks (`io.rs:312`). A file of about 4,096 one-CC tracks (around 50 KB) now creates 4,096 synth tracks, where before it created none.
- **Fix:** `MAX_MIDI_TEMPOS` (10k) and `MAX_MIDI_TRACKS` (512), checked before mutation; collapse equal tempos; long term, cumulative offsets with a binary search in `TempoMap`. A fix was proposed in #750 (closed unmerged).

title: [Audit] The web build has no panic containment
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

- **Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** Confirmed for platform semantics; Plausible for specific panics. #897 is a concrete one.
- **Evidence:**
  - `wasm32-unknown-unknown` uses `panic=abort`, so `engine/src/lib.rs:319, 358` and `symph::guarded` (`audio-io/src/symph.rs:35-37`) do nothing there.
  - Video decodes inline on the UI thread (`ui-egui/src/video_track.rs:217-235`).
  - `MAX_RENDER_SAMPLES = 1 << 29` (`mix/src/lib.rs:2038`): a mono `vec![0.0f32; 1<<29]` is 2 GiB, more than `isize::MAX` on wasm32.
  - The web shell now records undo on success (`apps/soundcraft-web/src/web.rs:168-190`), but still calls `io::import_*_bytes` directly (#911).
- **Fix:** use 32-bit caps (`cfg(target_pointer_width = "32")`), decode in a Web Worker, document that restore-on-panic is native only, and fuzz with `-C panic=abort`.

title: [Audit] Session JSON has no size cap and is parsed into a `Value` first
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/io.rs:40-48`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L40-L48)

- **Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** Confirmed for no cap and the double parse; Plausible for the factor.
- **Evidence:** `crates/engine/src/io.rs:40-48` (`std::fs::read` with no limit); `open_session_linked` (`:1156-1158`); `model/src/session.rs:535-544`:
  ```rust
  let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(text)...;
  ...
  let mut s: Session = serde_json::from_value(v)...;
  ```
- the model has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so an unknown key holding `[0,0,0,…]` is fully materialised in the `Value` tree, at about 32 bytes of `Value` per 2 input bytes. That is roughly 16×.
- **Fix:** cap at about 256 MiB from `metadata().len()`. Parse the version with a tiny `struct Head { format_version: Option<Value> }` (other fields are skipped, not kept), then call `from_str::<Session>` directly.

title: [Audit] WAV parsing is quadratic in the number of empty `data` chunks
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

Regression introduced by the fix for #466 (7f2ff83).

**Code:** [`crates/audio-io/src/wav.rs:146-165, 198-199`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/audio-io/src/wav.rs#L146-L165)

- **Severity:** Medium (a hang, with no crash or data loss beyond the frozen app). **Confidence:** **Confirmed, reproduced.** **Introduced by** 7f2ff83, "WAV: an empty data chunk followed by metadata has no frames (#466)".

**Evidence:** in `crates/audio-io/src/wav.rs:198-199`, inside the main chunk loop:
```rust
let finished = u64::from(le_u32(b, 4).unwrap_or(0)) + 8 == b.len() as u64;
let empty = size32 == 0 && !is_rf64 && finished && only_chunks_follow(b, body);
```
- `only_chunks_follow` (`:146-165`) walks every chunk to the end of the file, with no limit.
- It runs for **every** zero-size `data` chunk, although only the first is used (`if data.is_none()`).
- An empty chunk advances `pos` by only 8 bytes, so the outer loop, capped at 100,000 chunks, calls it again and again.

**Reproduction.** A crate outside the repo, built `--release`. The file is `RIFF` + `fmt ` + N × `data\0\0\0\0` + M × `junk\0\0\0\0`, with a correct RIFF size, passed to `soundcraft_audio_io::probe(&f, Some("wav"))`:
```
data=10000  junk=0      bytes=80036    probe=Ok(()) took=87.34ms
data=30000  junk=0      bytes=240036   probe=Ok(()) took=785.03ms
data=100000 junk=0      bytes=800036   probe=Ok(()) took=9.06s
data=99990  junk=400000 bytes=3999956  probe=Ok(()) took=88.43s
```
The time grows quadratically and is still unbounded in M: a 16 MB file is several minutes.

**Reachability:**
- `wav::parse` is reached through `probe` and `decode` (`audio-io/src/lib.rs:213, 233`).
- Callers: `file.import_audio`, session and bundle open (`decode_source`), clip-group import (`clip_group_file.rs:116`), take decoding, and web import.

**Impact:**
- Import freezes the UI thread.
- A shared session r…

title: [Audit] Offline-render commands have no total budget; duplicate track ids multiply it
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/cmd/audiosuite.rs:141-160, 62-131`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/cmd/audiosuite.rs#L141-L160)

- **Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code.
- **Evidence:**
  - Each render is capped at `render_limit` (2^29 f32 = 2 GiB). But commands loop over tracks or clips and **keep** every result as a new pool source, which undo snapshots also hold.
  - `tracks_param` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs:223-235`) does not remove duplicates.
  - The `audiosuite.process` signal-generator branch (`cmd/audiosuite.rs:141-160`) checks per track only:
    ```rust
    crate::io::refuse_longer(e.session(), "audiosuite.process", &t.name, "generate on", r.len(), crate::io::render_limit(t.channels()))?;
    ...
    let mut audio = vec![vec![0.0; frames]; channels];
    ```
  - The same pattern appears in the `audiosuite.process` per-clip loop (`:62-131`; each clip is rendered twice, about 4 GiB peak), `track.commit` (`cmd/track.rs:818` → `io::commit_track`, `io.rs:827-865`) and `edit.consolidate` (`edit.rs:949-962`).
- **Scenarios:**
  - **MCP or control channel:** one `audiosuite.process` signal-generator call that lists the same track id eight times over a range of about 3 hours keeps about 16 GiB, and the process aborts.
  - **Hostile session:** 16 mono clips of about 3 h each over a 1-frame WAV; select all and run AudioSuite Gain; about 32 GiB, abort.
- **Fix sketch:**
  ```diff
   // tracks_param
  +        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
  +        out.retain(|t| seen.insert(*t));
   // per command
  +    let mut budget = MAX_RENDER_SAMPLES;
  +    budget = budget.checked_sub(frames * channels).ok_or_else(|| bad(cmd, "too much audio in one command"))?;
  ```
  Long term, add a per-session pool byte budget (the same fix direction as #882).

title: [Audit] H.264 `mb_skip_run` bounds check wraps on 32-bit targets
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/video/src/h264/slicedec.rs:1446-1447`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/video/src/h264/slicedec.rs#L1446-L1447)

- **Severity:** Medium; High for the web build. Native 64-bit is not affected. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code.
- **Evidence:** `crates/video/src/h264/slicedec.rs:1440-1452`:
  ```rust
  let run = r.read_ue()? as usize;
  ensure!(addr + run <= total, "mb_skip_run out of range");
  for _ in 0..run {
      self.start_mb(addr);            // indexes self.pic.mbs[addr]
  ```
  `read_ue` (`crates/video/src/bitstream.rs:119-133`) accepts 32 leading zeros, so it can return `u32::MAX`.
- **Scenario:** in a CAVLC P slice at `addr >= 1` (a run of 0, one coded MB, then a run of `u32::MAX`), `addr + run` wraps to a small number on wasm32. The check passes, and the loop indexes `pic.mbs[total]`. That is a panic, which is an abort on wasm (#891). In debug builds the `+` itself panics.
- **Impact:** any imported or session-referenced MP4/MOV kills the web app's tab.
- **Fix:**
  ```diff
  -ensure!(addr + run <= total, "mb_skip_run out of range");
  +ensure!(run <= total - addr, "mb_skip_run out of range"); // addr < total is checked just above
  ```
- **Test:** factor out `skip_run_fits(addr, run, total)` and assert `!skip_run_fits(1, usize::MAX, 99)`. This is portable, since `usize::MAX` on 64-bit plays the role of `u32::MAX` on 32-bit.

title: [Audit] Unpinned appimagetool from the `continuous` tag
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`packaging/linux/package.sh:114-120`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/packaging/linux/package.sh#L114-L120)

- **Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** Confirmed. That the embedded runtime also comes from `continuous` is Plausible.
- **Evidence:** `packaging/linux/package.sh:114-120`:
  ```sh
  curl --proto '=https' -fsSL -o "$TOOL" "https://github.com/AppImage/appimagetool/releases/download/continuous/appimagetool-$ARCH.AppImage"
  ```
  - 9b8283b added only `--proto`; there is no version pin and no checksum.
  - `SHA256SUMS.txt` is computed afterwards, so it cannot catch a tampered tool.
  - A stale `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/appimagetool-*` is reused without a check.
- **Impact:** whoever controls that release asset controls code that runs in the release job and the runtime shipped inside every AppImage.
- **Fix:** pin a tag, verify with `sha256sum -c` against a committed hash, and pass a pinned, verified `--runtime-file`.

title: [Audit] No CI gate on PRs; grouped daily dependency bumps
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`.github/dependabot.yml:11-14`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/.github/dependabot.yml#L11-L14)

- **Severity:** Medium (it enables #880). **Confidence:** Confirmed.
- **Evidence:**
  - `.github/workflows/` has `freebsd`, `nix`, `packaging-lint`, `release`, `sonarcloud` and `windows-arm64`. No workflow runs `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm), and git history shows none ever did.
  - FreeBSD tests run only nightly, on `release`, or for PRs touching playback or FreeBSD packaging. There is no `cargo audit` or `cargo deny`.
  - `.github/dependabot.yml:11-14` groups every crate (`patterns: ["*"]`) into one daily PR, and 7b339fe makes CodeRabbit skip Dependabot PRs.

- **Fix:** a PR workflow running `cargo xtask ci` and `cargo deny check advisories bans sources`, required on `main`, plus a scheduled `cargo audit`. Split the Dependabot groups (security updates separate from version bumps).

title: [Audit] clap-host `on_main_thread()` is a stub off macOS
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/clap-host/src/ffi.rs:727-730`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/clap-host/src/ffi.rs#L727-L730)

- **Severity:** Low-Medium.
- **Confidence:** the defect is confirmed; the crash is Plausible.
- **Evidence:** `crates/clap-host/src/ffi.rs:727-730`:
  ```rust
  #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
  pub(crate) fn on_main_thread() -> bool { true }
  ```
  `GuiLink::kill` (`:1025-1037`) relies on it.
- **When it matters:** the `garbage` channel is unbounded (`playback/src/lib.rs:535`), so `send` fails only if the receiver was dropped. The realistic path is `Player` teardown:
  - `Player` has no `Drop`, and its fields drop in declaration order (`:456-476`), so `side` (the garbage receiver) drops before `_stream`;
  - the cpal callback closure, with every plugin, is then dropped on the backend's thread (WASAPI, ALSA).
- **Mitigation present:** `ui-egui/src/lib.rs:810, 906` call `close_editors()` before replacing the Player.
- **Fix:** `std::thread::current().name() == Some("main")`, the same rule as `hostwin` and vst3-host, or record the main thread's id at startup.

title: [Audit] VST3 bus tables still truncated to 16 (CLAP fixed)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

- **Fix:** report a problem that lists the kept paths, and call `sync_all()` on finish.
