title: [Audit] Clip-multiplying edits end in a quadratic hang
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:583-598`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs#L583-L598)

- **Severity:** Low-Medium. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code; timing estimated.
- **Evidence:**
  - `edit.repeat` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:583-598`, `count.clamp(1, 999)`) pastes every clip in range `count` times.
  - `clip.loop` (`cmd/clip.rs:288-315`) does up to 1,000 repetitions.
  - Each paste goes through `place_clip` (`edit.rs:210-216`): an O(N) `clear_range` plus a sort.
  - There is no cap on clips per playlist.
- **Scenario:** repeat one clip 999×, select all, repeat 999× again: 10^6 placements of O(N) cost each, about 5×10^11 steps. The engine/UI thread hangs for hours, and undo snapshots and autosave double the memory.
- **Also quadratic:** `create_fades` (`edit.rs:796`, `xfaded.contains`) and `midi.note_delete` / `midi.notes_move` (`cmd/midi.rs:113-131`, `idx.contains(&i)`).
- **Fix:** cap the clips a command may create (for example 100,000 per playlist, refused before mutating), batch the pastes (clear once, sort once), and use a `HashSet` for index lists.

---
_Audit ref: `L-15`._

title: [Audit] Release builds restore caches that unprotected `main` can write
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

- **Severity:** Low-Medium. **Confidence:** Plausible.
- **Evidence:** release jobs use `Swatinem/rust-cache` with `key: release-<platform>` (`craft-common-actions release.yml:216, 351, 457, 943, 1006`). The `release` branch can restore caches created on the default branch.
- **Impact:** poisoned `.rlib` files or build-script outputs can reach signed binaries without ever appearing in the `release` branch.
- **Fix:** no build cache in signing jobs (or lookup-only), and protect `main`.

---
_Audit ref: `L-16`._

title: [Audit] Backup rotation trusts names planted in `Backups/`
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

Related: #426.

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/io.rs:1078-1093`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L1078-L1093)

- **Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code.
- **Evidence:** `crates/engine/src/io.rs:1078-1093`:
  ```rust
  let Some(next) = numbers.iter().max().map_or(Some(1), |n| n.checked_add(1)) else {
      log::warn!("no backup of {}: backup numbers are exhausted", file.display());
      return;
  };
  ```
  Pruning removes every `n` with `n + 10 <= next`.
- **Scenario:** a shared project folder carries `Song backup 4294967295.scraft`, which turns backups off silently and permanently. With `…4294967285`, the next save prunes every real backup.
- **Incomplete fix:** 75eb152's `create_new` protects only the final component. A symlinked `Backups/` folder is still followed by `create_dir_all`, by the copy and by `remove_file`.
- **Fix:** choose `next` from the contiguous run the app wrote, prune only within a bounded range, and refuse when `symlink_metadata(&backups)` is a link.

---
_Audit ref: `L-17`._

title: [Audit] The output NaN guard covers only the mono-device path
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/playback/src/lib.rs:366, 388-396`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/playback/src/lib.rs#L366)

- **Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Plausible.
- **Evidence:** `crates/playback/src/lib.rs:386-396`:
  ```rust
  if mono.is_finite() { mono } else { 0.0 }     // mono device (516ef23)
  0 => l.clamp(-1.0, 1.0),                       // NaN.clamp(..) is NaN
  *o = if c < nch.max(1) && sounding { sample(c).clamp(-1.0, 1.0) } else { 0.0 };
  ```
  The interpolation `a + (b - a) * fr` (`:366`) is NaN when `b - a` overflows to ±inf and `fr = 0`: two adjacent finite samples near ±3.4e38, which `contain_failure` lets through.
- **Fix:** one helper, `let o = v.clamp(-1.0, 1.0); if o.is_finite() { o } else { 0.0 }`, for all branches. Or interpolate as `a * (1.0 - fr) + b * fr`.

---
_Audit ref: `L-18`._

title: [Audit] Failed-insert latency exclusion re-runs the delay-line reallocation in the callback
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/mix/src/lib.rs:1652`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/mix/src/lib.rs#L1652)

- **Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code.
- **Evidence:** `crates/mix/src/lib.rs:1652` (`|| slot.failed`, ef65cea).
- **Mechanism:** a plugin that fails mid-playback lowers the latency. `MixEngine::reset` (`:502-507`, on stop or locate) clears `failed`, the plugin fails again, and the latency changes back. Every change runs `DelayLine::set`'s full reallocation (#889) on the audio thread.
- **Fix:** the #889 fix (pre-sized lines), or debounce the retry for plugins that keep failing.

---
_Audit ref: `L-19`._

title: [Audit] A punch that misses the take mutates the session with no undo step
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/io.rs:1461-1490`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L1461-L1490)

- **Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code.
- **Evidence:** `crates/engine/src/io.rs:1461-1490`. `add_source` runs before the per-pass loop. When `Range::new(start, start+n).intersect(&p)` is `None` for every pass, nothing is placed and `push_undo` never runs, but the source stays in the pool (marked unsaved) and is saved with the session.
- **Fix:** compute the intersections first; call `add_source` only if a clip will be placed.

---
_Audit ref: `L-20`._

title: [Audit] `MAX_MEASURES` does not bound Print Score output
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/score.rs:15, 410-420`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/score.rs#L15)

- **Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code; the size estimate is computed.
- **Evidence:** `crates/engine/src/score.rs:14-15` says "MAX_MEASURES so a hostile session cannot make a huge document", but nothing bounds the items per measure (up to 1,024 sixteenths) or the pitches per chord (up to 128). The ledger-line loop (`:410-420`) emits about 20 `<line>` elements for an extreme pitch, roughly 2 KB of SVG per note against about 40 bytes of JSON in the session.
- **Scenario:** a 10 M-note session gives a ~20 GB `String` and an abort, through `write_score` (`cmd/file.rs:320-334`). MusicXML is about 250 B per note.
- **Fix:** a byte budget in `svg`/`musicxml` (for example 256 MiB, then "score too large"), and a notes-per-part cap in `layout`.

---
_Audit ref: `L-21`._

title: [Audit] `normalize` divides by a subnormal peak
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/dsp/src/offline.rs:72-77`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/dsp/src/offline.rs#L72-L77)

- **Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code.
- **Evidence:** `crates/dsp/src/offline.rs:72-77`:
  ```rust
  let p = peak(ch);
  if p > 0.0 { let g = target / p; ch.iter_mut().flatten().for_each(|s| *s *= g); }
  ```
  With a peak around 1e-40, `g` is infinite: nonzero samples become ±inf and zeros become NaN. AudioSuite Normalize stores the result as a new source.
- **Fix:** `if p > 1e-20 { let g = (target / p).min(db_to_gain(144.0)); … }`.
- **Test:** `normalize(&mut [vec![1e-40, 0.0]], 0.0, false)` must leave every value finite.

---
_Audit ref: `L-22`._

title: [Audit] `relink_videos` hands the UI an unchecked raw path
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/io.rs:265-281`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L265-L281)

- **Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code.
- **Evidence:** `crates/engine/src/io.rs:265-281`. When `stored_path` resolves but the file is missing:
  ```rust
  (None, Ok(p)) => missing.push(format!("{} (video)", p.display())),
  ```
  `v.path` keeps the **raw** stored string and `v.offline` stays `None`. The video worker later opens it as given (`ui-egui/src/video_track.rs:95`, `File::open(path)`), relative to the process working directory rather than the session folder.
- **Impact:** this breaks the rule that every session path goes through `stored_path` before touching the filesystem.
- **Fix:** store the resolved path (or set `offline`) in that arm, and make the UI honour `offline`.

---
_Audit ref: `L-23`._

title: [Audit] `ui.set` saves unchecked UI state; Workspace runs `read_dir` every frame
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:666-686`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs#L666-L686)

- **Severity:** Low (needs #877 or a hand-edited `ui.json`). **Confidence:** Confirmed by code.
- **Evidence:**
  - `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:666-686` merges any JSON into `UiState`, checking only docking, and saves it to `ui.json`. `recent_sessions` is not capped at `MAX_RECENT`, and `workspace_dir` and `window_size` are taken as given.
  - `crates/ui-egui/src/windows.rs:325-347` calls `std::fs::read_dir(&dir)` and a full sort **every frame** while the Workspace window is open.
- **Scenario:** a `ui.set` over the control channel sets `workspace_dir` to a UNC path and opens the Workspace window. On Windows every frame opens SMB to the attacker (NTLM) and blocks the UI thread, and the setting persists across restarts. Even without an attacker, a 1 M-entry folder freezes the UI.
- **Fix:** cache the listing (refresh it off-thread on navigation), refuse UNC paths lexically, and validate `UiState` after deserializing.

---
_Audit ref: `L-24`._

title: [Audit] Autosave recovery deleted on an mtime comparison
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/autosave.rs:268-282`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/autosave.rs#L268-L282)

- **Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Plausible.
- **Evidence:** `crates/engine/src/autosave.rs:268-282`:
  ```rust
  Ok(saved) if recording || origin_saved.is_none_or(|o| saved > o) => { … offer recovery … }
  _ => { let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir); }
  ```
  If the origin file's mtime is newer for any reason other than a save (a sync client touching it, clock skew on a share, `touch`), the unsaved work is deleted at startup without asking.
- **Fix:** delete only when the autosave's content matches the saved file (for example a hash recorded at save time); otherwise offer recovery.

---
_Audit ref: `L-25`._

title: [Audit] Unbounded command journal
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:339-341`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L339-L341)

- **Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code.
- **Evidence:** `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:339-341`:
  ```rust
  if spec.journal { self.journal.push((id.to_string(), params.clone())); }
  ```
  It is never trimmed, so large params (`clips`/`indices` arrays, junk fields from MCP or the control channel) are kept for the life of the process.
- **Fix:** a ring buffer (for example the last 10,000 entries) with a per-entry size cap.

---
_Audit ref: `L-26`._

title: [Audit] H.264 arithmetic that overflows on crafted streams
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/video/src/h264/transform.rs:101-124, 141-158`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/video/src/h264/transform.rs#L101-L124)

- **Severity:** Low (it panics in debug and overflow-checks builds and aborts in wasm debug builds; release builds just decode garbage). **Confidence:** Confirmed by code.
- **IDCT:** `crates/video/src/h264/transform.rs:101-124` (`idct4_add`) and `:141-158` (`idct8_1d`) use plain `+`/`-` on coefficients that `scale4`/`scale8` (`:35, :41`) deliberately produce with `wrapping_mul … <<`.
- **Temporal direct:** `slicedec.rs:606-608` computes `[m0[0] - mv_col[0], m0[1] - mv_col[1]]` as i16.
- **Fix:** clamp dequantised values to ±2^15 (spec 8.5.12.1), and compute motion vectors in i32 and clamp them to the spec range.
- **Test:** `idct4_add(&[i32::MAX; 16], &mut [0; 16], 4)` must not panic in debug.

---
_Audit ref: `L-27`._

title: [Audit] H.264 arithmetic that overflows on crafted streams
author: PierrunoYT

- **Temporal direct:** `slicedec.rs:606-608` computes `[m0[0] - mv_col[0], m0[1] - mv_col[1]]` as i16.
- **Fix:** clamp dequantised values to ±2^15 (spec 8.5.12.1), and compute motion vectors in i32 and clamp them to the spec range.

title: [Audit] `file.export_session_text` overwrites without a replace guard
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:113-119`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L113-L119)

- **Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Confirmed by code.
- **Evidence:** `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:113-119`:
  ```rust
  if let Some(path) = str_param(p, "path") { crate::io::write_file(path, text.as_bytes())?; }
  ```
  `session.save_as` goes through `refuse_replacing` (`:200-207`); this command does not. An agent confined to a write root can silently clobber any existing file inside it, and under #877 any file at all.
- **Fix:** require `replace: true` to overwrite, as `save_as` does.

_Audit ref: `L-28`._

title: [Audit] Smaller CI secret-handling issues
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

**Code:** [`.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml:19-20`](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/9b8283b90877813a929f5e28b2dc92e5774da933/.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml#L19-L20)

- **Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Confirmed for the config.
- **`secrets: inherit` at `@main`:** `.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml:19-20` passes every secret it can see to a reusable workflow at `@main`, and it runs on every push to `main` and every same-repo PR. Per `gh api`, the signing secrets are environment-scoped and so are not inherited. Repo- and org-level secrets could not be listed (403). **Fix:** pass only `SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}`, and pin by SHA.
- **Script injection:** `craft-common-actions/actions/resolve-version/action.yml:37` does `v="${{ inputs.input-version }}"`, script injection from a `workflow_dispatch` input. Only writers can trigger it, in a read-only job. **Fix:** go through `env:`.
- **Secrets on command lines:**
  - `packaging/macos/package.sh:86, 93` (`notarytool --password "$APPLE_PASSWORD"`)
  - `packaging/windows/sign.ps1:69` (`/p $env:WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`)
  - `packaging/macos/import-cert.sh:30` (`-P "$APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD"`)

  **Fix:** a `notarytool` keychain profile, and signing by store thumbprint.

---
_Audit ref: `L-29`._

body:

- No `fuzz/` directory.
- No PR CI (#900).

title: [Audit] Automation roots confine files, not plugins
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Found in a security and robustness audit of `main` at 9b8283b (0.11.0).

- **Severity:** Info.

Under `soundcraft-cli mcp --automation-*-root`, the agent can still run:
- `engine.vst3_plugins {"rescan":true}` and `engine.clap_plugins`;
- `mix.insert {"plugin":"clap:…"}` followed by a bounce.

title: Add support for opencode and make them skills — the SoundCraft agent skill
author: AHL8192
body:
**What**

There is no OpenCode skill for SoundCraft yet, while sibling craft apps (photocraft, vectorcraft, filmcraft, designcraft, pdfcraft, effectcraft, gridcraft, deckcraft, wordcraft, figcraft, photocraft...) have one. SoundCraft is the odd one out of the audio-sibling group.

SoundCraft is "an open-source, clean-room reimplementation of Avid Pro Tools in pure Rust" (3.5K ⭐). Its philosophy: **everything is a command** — engine.execute, menus, UI_COMMANDS. The headless "soundcraft-cli mcp" and "--demo --control 0" control channel (port printed) mean the work is already done — what's missing is an OpenCode skill that turns its AGENTS.md doc into an operating manual for agents: command vocabulary, coordinates (ticks/seconds?), traps (the control port), recipes (demo, bounce, screenshot).

**Ask**
- Add an OpenCode skill for SoundCraft that turns the existing docs into an operating manual:
  - MCP tool list + when to use control channel vs MCP (soundcraft-cli mcp [--connect PORT], control port printed from --demo --control 0)
  - Command vocabulary: engine command ids, UI_COMMANDS, menu dispatch
  - Coordinates: time in seconds/ticks? audio device params, peaks, db
  - Recipes: demo session, bounce, plugin params
  - Never-crash rules from AGENTS.md

**Tags:** feature, skill, opencode, automation

title: Linux: the System theme never follows the desktop (always dark)
author: craptocracy
body:
## What happens

In **Setup › Appearance**, the **System** theme is meant to follow the desktop's light or dark setting. On Linux it always shows the Dark palette: with the desktop switched to light mode, SoundCraft stays dark, and restarting SoundCraft doesn't change that. Choosing **Light** or **Dark** directly works.

## Environment

- Linux Mint 22.3, Cinnamon, X11
- SoundCraft v0.12.1 (the latest release)
- The desktop's Settings portal reports the mode correctly (`1` = dark, `2` = light):

```console
$ gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop --object-path /org/freedesktop/portal/desktop --method org.freedesktop.portal.Settings.ReadOne org.freedesktop.appearance color-scheme
(<uint32 2>,)
```

## Cause

https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft/blob/06db0bd3733075626f4062ed8efccbb8ec117e38/crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs#L396-L403

`wants_light()` resolves System only from `ctx.system_theme()`. That value comes from eframe/winit, which reports no system theme on Linux or the BSDs (see storytold/figcraft#622), so it is always `None` there and System falls through to Dark. #85 lists that fallback ("OS unavailable -> Dark fallback"), but on Linux the OS appearance is never available. Nothing in the app asks the desktop directly.

## Suggested fix

When `ctx.system_theme()` is `None`, read the Settings portal's `org.freedesktop.appearance` / `color-scheme` (1 = dark, 2 = light, 0 = no preference) and follow its `SettingChanged` signal. Several Craft apps already do this, for example [CADCraft's `desktop_theme.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/main/apps/cadcraft/src/desktop_theme.rs), [LightCraft's `appearance.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/main/apps/lightcraft/src/appearance.rs) and the shared [`craft-platform` appearance module](https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs/blob/main/crates/platform/src/appearance.rs) in craft-libs. FigCraft has the same gap, with a pending fix in storytold/figcraft#623.

title: Audio decoding bugs fixed (a crash, ADPCM accuracy, Vorbis channel order) and up to 1.24× faster decoding with house codecs
author: Ttimmahlax
body:
Hi SoundCraft team 👋

We make software and hardware for home devices. While using SoundCraft we swapped some of our house
technology in underneath it: a faster allocator, and pure-Rust audio and picture codecs.

Two things came out of it. First, the codec swap fixed several audio-decoding bugs on `main`,
including a crash. Second, parts of SoundCraft got faster, and a couple of other bugs turned up
along the way.

## The problems we fixed: audio files that crash, decode wrongly, or end late

Each one was checked against FFmpeg 8.1.2's decode.

1. **A crash.** symphonia panics on a truncated FLAC-in-Matroska file, against SoundCraft's
   never-crash rule. Our decode corpus of truncated copies of FFmpeg-made files found it; we haven't
   re-checked it by hand. With FLAC decoded by rusty_flac the file opens.
2. **IMA ADPCM WAV decodes up to 64 LSB16 away from FFmpeg** (symphonia's decoder). With the house
   decoder it is bit-exact.
3. **5.1 Vorbis comes out in the wrong channel order.** symphonia's 5.1 output matched FFmpeg in no
   channel order. It now comes out in WAV order, like every other format.
4. **Ogg and Matroska Vorbis files end late.**
   - symphonia ignores the Ogg end-granule trim and Matroska `DiscardPadding`, so files decode
     112–636 samples long. For example, a 1 s Ogg file gives 44,608 frames where FFmpeg gives 43,972.
   - Every count now equals FFmpeg's.
5. **Files that didn't open now do:** Opus and 5.1/PCE AAC.

On 97 test files, including truncated and corrupted copies, lengths and alignment match symphonia
apart from these fixes. FLAC is bit-exact; MP3 and AAC are within 1.5e-6; Vorbis matches FFmpeg's
float decode within 7.5e-8.

## The opportunity: faster editing and decoding with our crates

We changed **only dependencies**:

| was | now |
|---|---|
| system allocator (Windows heap) | **rusty_alloc**, in the program binaries only |
| `serde_json` | **rusty_json_turbo** (serde_json fork, byte-identical output), via one `[patch.crates-io]…

title: Hosted plug-in parameters: control the instrument slot, list parameters, set them by name
author: sanderdewijs
body:
## Summary

Third-party plug-in parameters (AU, VST3, CLAP) can only be set by id, there is no command that lists which parameters a plug-in exposes, and **a hosted instrument's parameters cannot be set at all**. Since SoundCraft has no Audio Unit editor views (#501), this makes AU instruments effectively opaque when driving SoundCraft through commands or the MCP server.

## What fails today (tested 2026-10-25, macOS, Ample Guitar SC `au:aumu:Agsc:Apsd` on an instrument track)

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `mix.insert_param {track, slot: "instrument", param: "1575", value: 1}` | `slot` must be 0..9 or a..j |
| `mix.instrument_param {track, param: "1575", value: 1}` | `au:aumu:Agsc:Apsd` is not a built-in instrument |
| `automation.set_point {param: "plugin:instrument:1575", …}` | unknown automation param |
| `mix.instrument_param {track, param: 1575, value: 1}` (number) | `param` required |

Only `mix.insert_state {slot: "instrument"}` (an opaque state blob) works.

## What the code already has

The hosts already read every parameter's name, range, unit and choice labels into `PluginInfo::params`, in plain values. The mixer already pushes a hosted instrument's stored `Insert.params` into the live plug-in (`apply_params(…, INSTRUMENT_SLOT, …)`). What's missing is the command surface:

- `insert_param` and `insert_params` only accept insert slots.
- `mix.instrument_param` only looks up built-in plug-ins.
- `AutoParam::Plugin` has no instrument variant.
- There is no query that returns a hosted plug-in's parameter table (`engine.plugins` only lists built-ins).

## Proposal, as three small PRs

1. **Instrument slot.** `mix.insert_param` and `mix.insert_params` accept `slot: "instrument"`. `mix.instrument_param` also works for hosted instruments. A new automation param `plugin:instrument:<id>` drives the instrument. A numeric `param` is accepted as well as the decimal string. Plug-in editor edits on the instrument are stored in the session too (they're dropped today), s…

title: macOS CLI can't load third-party Audio Units (signed without the library-validation entitlement)
author: sanderdewijs
body:
## Problem

The released macOS `soundcraft-cli` can't load third-party Audio Units. Offline renders through the CLI play every hosted AU instrument and effect as digital silence (−144 dB). Built-in plug-ins render normally, and nothing is reported.

## Cause

`packaging/macos/package.sh:213` signs the CLI with `--options runtime` but without `--entitlements`. Under the hardened runtime, library validation then refuses plug-ins signed by other teams. The app is signed with `packaging/macos/entitlements.plist` (lines 132–133), which includes `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation`, so the app loads them fine.

Checked on the 0.10.0 release:
- `codesign -dv ~/.local/bin/soundcraft-cli` → `flags=0x10000(runtime)`, no entitlements.
- `/Applications/SoundCraft.app` → `disable-library-validation` present.

## Repro (macOS, with a third-party AU instrument)

`soundcraft-cli run --in session.scraft --cmd 'mix.solo={"tracks":["<AU track>"],"value":true}' --bounce out.wav --start 95 --end 100` gives `peak_db: -144`. The same session plays in the app.

A copy of the same 0.10.0 CLI, ad-hoc re-signed with the runtime **and** that entitlement, renders the AU (−10.65 dBFS).

## Fix

Sign the CLI with the entitlements as well: `sign --options runtime --entitlements "$HERE/entitlements.plist" "$CLI_DIR/soundcraft-cli"`, or with a CLI-specific plist that holds only `disable-library-validation`. Ideally the CLI also says so when a hosted plug-in fails to load, instead of rendering silence.

title: transport.play {from} is ignored in the app: playback starts at the edit selection
author: sanderdewijs
body:
## Problem

`transport.play {from: position}` doesn't play from `from` in the app. Playback starts at the edit selection (insertion point) instead. This affects agents and scripts using the control channel or MCP. The CLI was not tested.

## Cause

The command pushes `TransportRequest::Locate(at)` and then `TransportRequest::Play` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/transport.rs:10-16`). In the UI, `Locate` sets `engine.transport.position` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1135`). `Play` then calls `play_from_selection()` (`lib.rs:1115`), which starts at the selection, so the located position is overwritten.

## Repro

Open a session whose insertion point is at 2:39 and send `{"method":"engine.execute","params":{"command":"transport.play","params":{"from":4560000}}}`. `ui.inspect` reports a position of about 160 s after one second, not about 96 s.

Workaround: `transport.play`, then `transport.locate {at}` while playing.

## Fix

When `from` is given, start playback at that position: a `PlayFrom(at)` request, or have `Play` honour a `Locate` from the same batch. Add a test that `transport.play {from}` starts at `from` regardless of the selection.

title: Solo: an aux fed by a soloed track stays audible; the incumbent mutes it unless it is Solo Safe
author: lucasegen
body:
Soloing a track keeps every aux it feeds audible, by its output or a send: reverb returns and submix auxes alike. The incumbent mutes them, and Solo Safe is how you keep one.

## Now (`main` @ 0a95b6d)
- `receives_solo` (`crates/mix/src/lib.rs:1561`) exempts from the solo any track whose input bus a soloed track feeds (`:1116`).
- `mix.solo_safe` exists (`crates/engine/src/cmd/mix.rs:22`) and the mixer honours it, but no click reaches it: `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/command_reachability.rs:25` lists it as a known gap.

## Incumbent
In the default solo mode, soloing a track mutes every track that is not soloed, auxes included: a vocal soloed with a post-fader send to a reverb plays dry. Cmd-click (Ctrl-click) on an aux's Solo button makes it Solo Safe, and it stays audible. Soloing a submix aux plays nothing, since its sources are muted. Only Routing Folders and VCA Masters carry a solo: a soloed member keeps its folder audible, and a soloed folder or VCA solos its members. Described in words only (clean-room rule).

## Proposal
1. Cmd/Ctrl-click on a Solo button toggles `mix.solo_safe`, shown on the button.
2. Keep the implicit solo for Folder tracks and VCAs only; an Aux track is muted by a solo unless it is Solo Safe.

## Question
Is this the behaviour you want? #800 (VCA solo, implicit solo along aux chains) would change with it: the chain part would apply to folders only.

I can open a PR once the direction is agreed.

title: audio-io: info reports more frames than the import decodes for AAC in MP4 (since 0.13)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version / OS:** SoundCraft 0.13.1 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11. 0.12.1 is correct.

**Steps**
1. Fixture [`fx_m4a_lastdur.m4a`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/soundcraft/fx_m4a_lastdur.m4a): 10 s, 48 kHz stereo AAC-LC in MP4, 470 packets, no edit list; the last sample's stts duration is 1145 instead of 1024 (phone recorders write it like that: the last sample lasts until the track end). Generator: [`make_info_length_fixtures.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/soundcraft/make_info_length_fixtures.py) (ffmpeg + Python standard library).
2. `soundcraft-cli info fx_m4a_lastdur.m4a`
3. `soundcraft-cli convert fx_m4a_lastdur.m4a out.wav --bit-depth 32f` (or `file.import_audio` in a session)

**Expected:** `info` gives the frames the import decodes: 481,280 (470 × 1024; ffmpeg decodes 481,280), as 0.12.1 does.

**Actual (0.13.1):** `info` reports 481,401 frames (the stts total); import and convert give 481,280.

**Where it seems to come from:** since #954, `info` takes the length from `Track::num_frames` (`crates/audio-io/src/symph.rs`), which the symphonia 0.6 MP4 reader fills with the stts total. Unchanged on main.

**Corpus:** in our corpus run (real-world phone videos), 13 AAC-in-MP4 tracks now get an `info` length 2.5 to 45 ms longer than the decoded audio.

*Tested and written by Claude (Anthropic). Posted for Udo Funk (@KNUFFIXX), emotional support human, who reads every report after it goes out.*

title: Agent-authored commits (Agent Studio series) vanish from contributor credit
author: arthur-drozdov
body:
## What happened

The Agent Studio series — 14 commits (`932e99f` … `ea87269`), merged into `main` around Oct 22 from the `claude/laughing-turing-7coocl` branch of `arthur-drozdov/soundcraft` — carries the author identity **`Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`** (Claude Code's default git identity) on every commit.

## Impact

- `contributors/contributors.json` keys its stats by GitHub login resolved from commit authors. `noreply@anthropic.com` resolves to no account, so those commits land **nowhere**: neither the human contributor nor "Claude" appears in About ▸ Contributors. (The file is also a snapshot from Oct 10 / release 0.5.0, so a regeneration is due regardless.)
- GitHub's contributor graph likewise shows zero commits for this work.
- The human who scoped, reviewed, and shipped the work (`arthur-drozdov`) has no attribution — even though AGENTS.md builds the entire credit model around "agents working for a contributor."

## Why it matters here

AGENTS.md's "Contributor credits" section assumes agent-written work is attributed to a human: `contributors.py` re-verifies who wrote each `people.toml` entry, and About ▸ Contributors/Models is compiled from these files. The About ▸ Models list already acknowledges Claude models — so the project clearly wants honest AI attribution; it's the **human** half of the attribution that silently disappears when the tool's default git identity leaks into the author field.

## Suggestions

1. **Convention for agent-driven PRs:** commit author = the human, with the tool as a co-author trailer (`Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`). Both get credit, the stats pipeline works, and AGENTS.md's "never add/edit anyone else's entry" rule stays intact.
2. **Guard rail:** have the contributors script (or `--check`) warn when commit authors don't resolve to a GitHub login, so this can't silently recur.
3. **One-off fix for the merged series:** I'll open a PR adding my own self-authored `[people.arthur-drozdov]` entry in `contri…

title: refactor(cli): parse `soundcraft-cli` arguments with clap, following RFC-0012
author: 1Git2Clone
body:
Move `soundcraft-cli`'s argument parsing to [clap](https://docs.rs/clap) derive and [thiserror](https://docs.rs/thiserror), the way photocraft did, so it follows [RFC-0012: Command-line conventions](https://github.com/storytold/craft-contrib/pull/18). Then every Craft CLI behaves the same: the same exit codes, help, errors, environment variables, completions and man pages.

## Reference

- **The rules:** [RFC-0012](https://github.com/storytold/craft-contrib/pull/18).
- **The plan and decisions:** [photocraft#7071](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/7071). It covers what was decided and why, such as rejecting repeated flags, `--version` with no `version` subcommand, and values that start with `-`.
- **The code:**
  - the port, merged as one PR: [photocraft#9167](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/9167);
  - its review follow-up, typed usage errors: [photocraft#9194](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/9194);
  - the ast-grep rules for the CLI code: [photocraft#9750](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/9750), using craft-common-actions' [`ast-grep.yml`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions/pull/80).
- **Files to read in photocraft:**
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/src/args.rs`
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/src/error.rs`
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/src/lib.rs` (`run`)
  - `crates/automation/src/args.rs` (shared flags and environment variables)
  - `apps/photocraft/src/launch_args.rs` (the desktop app)
  - `apps/photocraft-cli/examples/man-and-completions.rs`
  - `lint/ast-grep/`

## Scope

- [ ] Parse every subcommand into clap derive types with typed values. Unknown or repeated flags, bad values and conflicting flags become usage errors (exit 2, on stderr) before any work starts.
- [ ] Use thiserror enums for errors, including the usage errors clap can't express itself. No `Result<_, String>` or `format!` messages.
- [ ] `main` passes `args_os()` to `run(args, out, err) -> exit code`, and the tests call `run` directly.

title: I/O  input device's real channel count
author: vlada-jerkovic
body: I have TASCAM US-16x08 sound card. 16 Inputs and 8 outputs. WASAPI I/O is showing only In 1-8. It's a limit in SoundCraft's software. The driver isn't the cause, at least not of the "In 1-8" list itself. What's limiting it 1. **The input menu is hard-coded to 8 entries.** In crates/ui-egui/src/mix_window.rs:1365, route_menu builds the input list with for i in 1..=8. The comment above it even says "inputs 1-8". It never asks the device how many channels it has, so a 16-input card, a 2-input card and a 64-input card all show In 1-8. 2. Outputs aren't listed per channel at all. The output menu shows only the main output (Out 1-2 or the first entry in session.outputs) plus buses. Hardware outputs 3-8 can't be picked there. - WASAPI (the default build): what you get depends on how TASCAM's WDM driver presents the card. These drivers often show it as several stereo-pair devices instead of one 16-channel device. In that case you'd only get 2 channels from whichever pair is the default. - ASIO shows the US-16x08 as a single device with all 16 inputs and 8 outputs. SoundCraft has an opt-in asio feature for this: `cargo build -p soundcraft --features asio`. It needs the Steinberg ASIO SDK and LLVM/libclang. Then choose ASIO as the audio system. So even with the menu fixed, you'd want an ASIO build to reach all 16 inputs on that card. Can you make the input menu show In **1 to N** using the selected input device's real channel count, and add per-channel and per-pair hardware outputs to the output menu, with tests?

title: Flatpak: Record silently does nothing when the session was opened via the file chooser (document portal hides the session folder)
author: infinityespi
body:
## Summary

On the Linux Flatpak, recording fails silently when the session was opened through the file chooser. Pressing Record (with an armed track) does nothing: no take, no error. The same session records normally when the app is given access to the session's folder.

## Environment

- SoundCraft 0.13.1, Flatpak `ai.storyteller.soundcraft` (stable, user install)
- Fedora 44, GNOME on Wayland, PipeWire
- Session on an external drive (`/run/media/...`), outside the sandbox's default `xdg-music` access

## Steps to reproduce

1. Save a session somewhere outside `~/Music`.
2. Open it through the file chooser (or double-click the `.scraft` file).
3. Record-enable an audio track with a working input, then press Record (and Play).

**Expected:** a take is recorded into `Audio Files/` next to the session, or an error explains why it can't be.
**Actual:** nothing happens. No clip, no message, nothing in `soundcraft.log`.

## Cause

When the session comes in through the file chooser, the document portal exposes only that file, at `/run/user/1000/doc/<id>/<name>.scraft`. Its folder isn't visible, so the recorder can't create `Audio Files/` beside the session, and the failure is swallowed.

Confirmation: I relaunched the same session with `--filesystem=<session dir>`. Record then worked immediately (`transport.status` reported `recording: true`, and `Audio Files/Audio 1_01.wav` was written with real signal). The workaround is `flatpak override --user --filesystem=<drive or folder> ai.storyteller.soundcraft`.

## Suggested fix

- Surface the error. If the take folder can't be created or written, show a message instead of failing silently (related: #913).
- Handle portal-opened sessions. Detect a `/run/user/*/doc/` session path and ask for the session folder through the portal's directory chooser, or fall back to a writable recordings location and say so.
- Possibly ship broader filesystem access (e.g. `--filesystem=home`, plus removable media) like other Flatpak DAWs. Openin…
